item.title: LaMelo Ball lists $2.6 million luxury Charlotte condo after Timberwolves trade
item.description: LaMelo Ball lists $2.6 million luxury Charlotte condo after Timberwolves trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LaMelo Ball is officially moving on from Charlotte. The former Hornets star, 25, has listed his luxury uptown Charlotte condo for $2.6 million after being traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in a blockbuster deal in late June. According to Realtor.com , the 3,495-square-foot property features four bedrooms, four-and-a-half bathrooms, and some seriously luxurious amenities. Located inside The Trust, an exclusive seven-residence building in the heart of uptown Charlotte, the condo offers sweeping city views, soaring ceilings, and marble floors with gold detailing. There's also a gourmet kitchen with a massive waterfall island, a custom wet bar, and an elaborate dressing room that could rival a designer boutique. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Erika Mendoza Charlotte NC (@erika_lmendoza) "Some addresses speak for themselves. Others are reserved for those who value something extraordinary," Coldwell Banker real estate agent Erika Mendoza wrote on Instagram while promoting the luxury listing. RELATED: Devin Booker's Nike Book 2 sneakers get bold graffiti makeover LaMelo Ball's Charlotte condo has surprising connection to NFL star Cam Newton Before becoming an owner, Ball rented the unit from Carolina Panthers star Cam Newton . He later purchased the condo from the NFL quarterback for $2.47 million in 2024, according to the Charlotte Business Journal . He also purchased a second unit in the building on the floor below the property for $2.2 million, per Realtor. Newton isn't the only sports figure with ties to the upscale building. NBA legend and former Hornets minority owner Michael Jordan also owns property there. The listing comes as Ball prepares for his first season with the Timberwolves. The 2021 NBA Rookie of the Year spent six seasons with Charlotte before the June trade sent him and Josh Green to Minnesota in exchange for Naz Reid and future draft picks. item.title: Yankees Provide Injury Update On Aaron Judge
item.description: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge The New York Yankees played most of the season without Aaron Judge, who missed over 80 games with a rib injury and then suffered a calf strain after returning. Judge's late-season calf injury kept him out of the postseason as well. Now that the season is over, Judge will have time for his calf to heal, but general manager Brian Cashman provided an update on the three-time MVP. "We did exit interviews with everybody, obviously, including Aaron Judge. He was not available to us in the postseason. There was no, you know, there was no willy-nilliness over that. You know, he just wasn't physically able to post for us. So, because of the calf. In terms of the rib, we did the exit interviews, exit physicals, and that all came out fine for us. "And we do have a follow-up with the specialist, (Dr. Gregory Pearl), that has to take place still, just to be certain, because that's the expert in this field. And then once he weighs in, we'll have, you know, that all firmed up one way or the other. But as of right now, we feel like we're in a good place, and, you know, he can take advantage of the rest of the winter and be ready to go when spring training starts." Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! It sounds like the Yankees are expecting Judge to be at 100% by the start of spring training. Manager Aaron Boone also noted that there are no medical procedures currently scheduled for Yankees players. Losing Judge was a huge blow for the Yankees offense, and even when he did return from the rib injury, he injured his calf before he got his timing back. Getting Judge back at full strength will be key for the Yankees next year, but what will be more important is whether he can stay healthy. More MLB: Yankees' Hal Steinbrenner Responds To Aaron Judge's 'All In' Comment With Apparent Dig At Him

item.title: LeBron James Spars with Knicks Fans Before Scoring First Win with the 76ers
item.description: LeBron James Credit: Caleb Bowlin/Getty NEED TO KNOW LeBron James interacted with fans at Madison Square Garden The 76ers star was seen exchanging words with at least one fan, according to social media footage At another point in the game, James heard it from the crowd while he was at the free-throw line LeBron James appeared to give a fan an earful in the season-opener against the New York Knicks on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The Philadelphia 76ers star, 41, was seen interacting with at least one member of the crowd at Madison Square Garden during the second quarter. “Ain’t nothing soft in the Midwest,” James appeared to say, according to clips of the tiff . “I don’t know what the f--- you talking about.” He continued, “I’m not from the West Coast. I’m from Ohio. Baby, f--- is you talking about?!” NBC’s Mike Tirico seemed to have intel on the exchange, claiming that fans may have been taunting James over his helicopter commute from his home in New York City to Philly. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! At another point in the game, the former Lakers star got his own earful when he took to the free-throw line. LeBron James heart taunts from the crowd at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night. Credit: Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty In footage circulating on social media , fans chanted “We don’t want you.” The chirps appear to stem from remarks previously made by the NBA veteran, who contemplated joining the Knicks as a free agent. James signed a two-year, $8 million contract with Philadelphia over the summer after eight years with the Lakers. The NBA’s all-time leading scorer told ESPN last month that he once envisioned wrapping his storied NBA career in New York. James and the 76ers, however, got the last laugh Tuesday, spoiling the home team’s celebratory night — when Knicks players received their rings and unfurled the championship banner — with a 106-100 win. All of which had the NBA legend feeling generous in his comments after his regular-season debut for Philly. “It is a great night for New York fans, 50-plus years. I was a part of that at one point where we hadn’t won a major championship in Cleveland in over 50 years,” James told reporters . “The fans will never forget this moment, and will never forget that championship run. We’re happy just to be able to come and play on such a historical night in a historical building and play the game we love.” Read the original article on People

item.title: Samsung’s latest 55-inch Frame TV is down to its lowest price yet
item.description: Samsung’s latest version of The Frame TV is $400 off. | Image: Samsung If you want a TV but prefer something that won’t clash with your room’s decor, Samsung’s The Frame is a standout option that’s designed to look like a piece of framed art instead of a black, monolithic rectangle mounted to your wall. You can buy the latest version of the 55-inch Samsung Frame TV on sale for around $897.99 ($402 off) at Amazon , which marks a new low price. Larger sizes are on sale, too, including the new 98-inch model , which is down to $3,749.99 ($1,252 off). Samsung The Frame TV (2026) Where to Buy: $1097.99 $897.99 at Amazon (55-inch) The 2026 model is largely the same as its predecessor; The biggest hardware change is that this size of the TV features built-in ports instead of using Samsung’s One Connect Box. Like previous models, it has a matte, canvas-like display that more closely resembles an actual painting better than a glossy TV screen. Its built-in motion sensor detects when someone enters the room and can automatically display artwork, even adjusting its brightness and colors based on ambient lighting. It supports Samsung’s Art Store, which offers access to more than 5,000 works ranging from world-famous galleries to lesser known, independent artists. A full subscription costs $49.99 annually, though you can also enjoy 30 new free, rotating artworks every month. Samsung includes a wall mount and a black bezel in the box, with additional magnetic frame styles available separately to better match your space or taste. In terms of performance, the Frame prioritizes style over image quality, so it’s not necessarily the best choice for cinephiles who may be willing to pay more for a brighter picture, deeper blacks, and more lifelike colors. Still it offers a refresh rate of up to 144Hz with variable refresh rate support for smoother gaming, along with HDR10 Plus and Dolby Atmos support for a more immersive audio/visual experience. Read our Samsung The Frame (2025) comparison.

item.title: Brewers’ Brandon Woodruff Pitching To Jackson Chourio Before World Series Goes Viral (Watch)
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are just days away from the biggest series in franchise history, and one of their best players is doing everything he can to be part of it. With the World Series approaching, Brandon Woodruff took another major step in his comeback Tuesday, facing some of Milwaukee’s biggest bats in a live batting practice session at American Family Field. Among the hitters standing in the box was Jackson Chourio, the young Brewers star who has helped fuel Milwaukee’s postseason run. The session offered the team (and now the public) a closer look at Woodruff as manager Pat Murphy and the front office weigh one of their biggest roster decisions before Friday’s World Series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays. Below is the video. Also Read: WATCH: Packers Legend Mark Tauscher Yells “The Bears Still Suck” During Brewers’ NLCS Win Mar 31, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Brandon Woodruff (53) delivers a pitch against the Tampa Bay Rays in the fourth inning at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Brewers ‘ Brandon Woodruff Pitching Released To Public Woodruff’s appearance was captured on MLB Network’s GEICO Ballpark Cam, drawing attention from Brewers fans who have been waiting to see whether the veteran right-hander could make it back in time for the Fall Classic. According to MLB.com, Woodruff threw 23 live pitches and sat between 90 and 92 mph. He faced Chourio, Brice Turang, William Contreras and Christian Yelich before finishing his session against National League Championship Series MVP Jake Bauers. It was a significant moment for a pitcher whose season appeared to be over just a few months ago. Here is the video: Brandon Woodruff was seen throwing live at-bats on the @GEICO #BallparkCam #MLBTonight talks about what the team is looking for during the session as they decide on his roster status. https://t.co/2ejHQKaddC — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) October 20, 2026 Woodruff last pitched in a game on July 4, when his surgically repaired right shoulder began bothering him again. The injury initially put his season in serious doubt, with surgery scheduled for August. But his shoulder improved without another operation, allowing him to begin working toward a potential return. Since then, Woodruff has steadily increased his throwing workload, hoping to convince Milwaukee that he can contribute during the World Series. Tuesday’s session was particularly important because it marked his first time facing live hitters in nearly four months. The Brewers are not simply deciding whether Woodruff can throw. They also need to determine whether he can help them win against a Tampa Bay team that has earned its place in the championship series. It was a significant moment for a pitcher whose season appeared to be over just a few months ago. Here is the video: Brandon Woodruff was seen throwing live at-bats on the @GEICO #BallparkCam #MLBTonight talks about what the team is looking for during the session as they decide on his roster status. https://t.co/2ejHQKaddC — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) October 20, 2026 Woodruff last pitched in a game on July 4, when his surgically repaired right shoulder began bothering him again. The injury initially put his season in serious doubt, with surgery scheduled for August. But his shoulder improved without another operation, allowing him to begin working toward a potential return. Since then, Woodruff has steadily increased his throwing workload, hoping to convince Milwaukee that he can contribute during the World Series. Tuesday’s session was particularly important because it marked his first time facing live hitters in nearly four months. The Brewers are not simply deciding whether Woodruff can throw. They also need to determine whether he can help them win against a Tampa Bay team that has earned its place in the championship series. Woodruff understands the challenge facing both himself and the organization. After Tuesday’s workout, he acknowledged that the timing makes the decision difficult. “I know where I’m at. I’ve only faced live hitters once and the World Series starts in three days,” Woodruff told MLB.com. “As far as a decision, I haven’t heard anything. I’m sure they are discussing it.” That final decision is expected Friday morning, when Milwaukee must submit its World Series roster ahead of Game 1. The team will also want to see how Woodruff’s shoulder responds to the increased workload before making a commitment. Jul 21, 2025; Seattle, Washington, USA; Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Brandon Woodruff (53) throws against the Seattle Mariners during the second inning at T-Mobile Park. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images For the Brewers , there is an obvious appeal to having a pitcher with Woodruff’s experience available, even if his role would be limited. He has been a central figure in Milwaukee’s pitching staff for years, and his familiarity with the organization could be valuable during a series where every matchup matters. At the same time, the club cannot ignore the risk of adding a pitcher who has not appeared in a game since early July. A World Series roster spot is precious, and Milwaukee must be confident that Woodruff can handle the demands of postseason competition. Still, the fact that he has reached this point is encouraging. Not long ago, another major shoulder procedure appeared likely to end his season. Now, with the Brewers preparing for the World Series, he has given the organization a genuine decision to make. item.title: “You Should Be Embarrassed” – LA Radio Host Goes Scorched Earth on Randy Arozarena for Cheering Rays in ALCS While Mariners Missed Postseason
item.description: Randy Arozarena - Seattle Mariners | © Imagn LA radio host Steve Covino has criticized Randy Arozarena for cheering on his former team, the Tampa Bay Rays, during the ALCS while the Seattle Mariners watched the postseason from home. The Mariners endured a disappointing 2026 campaign, finishing with a losing record and missing the playoffs. Their season included a historic 22-0 defeat to the Milwaukee Brewers on August 18, the worst loss in franchise history. Seattle’s season ended on September 27 following a 7-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels. During the offseason, Arozarena, whose contract expires after the 2026 World Series, was spotted supporting Tampa Bay during its Game 6 victory over the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS on Monday. His appearance did not sit well with Covino, who called out the Mariners outfielder on a recent episode of “Covino & Rich.” “What are you doing at the game? What are you doing there? You should be embarrassed. You’re a spectator at a game you should be playing in,” Covino said. The radio host also criticized Arozarena’s interaction with Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero after the latter hit a crucial two-run home run. Caminero pointed toward Arozarena in the stands before sharing the outfielder’s signature arms-crossed celebration. Covino questioned the exchange and argued that Arozarena is still an employee. “The home run trot from Caminero. He rounds 3rd, but he stops at home plate right before he steps on home plate, and he looks into the crowd, folds his arms, stands still, looks into the crowd. Now what is he doing? He’s looking at Randy Arozarena, who’s doing it right back at him. I’m not mad at Caminero for posing towards Arozarena. I’m mad at Arozarena for being there in the first place. You’re still an employee.” Arozarena also attracted attention earlier in 2026 following a handshake controversy involving Mariners teammate Cal Raleigh during the World Baseball Classic. What did Randy Arozarena say about his controversy with Cal Raleigh? The incident occurred on March 9 during a pool-play game between Team USA and Team Mexico. When Arozarena stepped into the batter’s box for Mexico, he extended his hand toward Raleigh, who was catching for the United States. Raleigh did not reciprocate the gesture, as he didn’t want to fraternize with the opposite team. Arozarena subsequently criticized Raleigh during an interview with a Mexican journalist. He later apologized to his Mariners teammate, emphasizing that their relationship and shared goals remained intact ahead of the MLB season, as per MLB.com . “I understand that with Opening Day a few days away, I don’t want it to be a distraction. Cal and I have talked and I apologized for what I said after the game. Nothing in the WBC takes away from the fact that we are brothers and teammates. He’s family, and we are both focused on helping the Mariners win the World Series.” Arozarena played the 2026 MLB season under a one-year, $15.65 million contract with Sea

When Arozarena stepped into the batter’s box for Mexico, he extended his hand toward Raleigh, who was catching for the United States. Raleigh did not reciprocate the gesture, as he didn’t want to fraternize with the opposite team. Arozarena subsequently criticized Raleigh during an interview with a Mexican journalist. He later apologized to his Mariners teammate, emphasizing that their relationship and shared goals remained intact ahead of the MLB season, as per MLB.com . “I understand that with Opening Day a few days away, I don’t want it to be a distraction. Cal and I have talked and I apologized for what I said after the game. Nothing in the WBC takes away from the fact that we are brothers and teammates. He’s family, and we are both focused on helping the Mariners win the World Series.” Arozarena played the 2026 MLB season under a one-year, $15.65 million contract with Seattle after agreeing to the deal in January to avoid arbitration. item.title: Fantasy football injury report: Latest Week 7 updates on Lamar Jackson, Quinshon Judkins
item.description: Another week in the NFL, another round of injuries . Several key players, including Davante Adams , Romeo Doubs and Terry McLaurin suffered significant injuries in Week 6 that will sideline them for an extended period. At least fantasy football managers know they need to find immediate replacements there. The guys who are questionable, but could play this week are the ones who are most concerning right now. Here are some of the most prominent players dealing with nagging ailments or returning from major issues that will impact fantasy managers most in Week 7. As always, keep an eye on the latest developments leading up to kickoff with our player notes page . WEEK 7 BYES: Buffalo, Jacksonville, L.A. Chargers, Washington WEEK 7 RANKINGS: QB | RB | WR | TE | K | DST | FLEX QB Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens Jackson is still technically day-to-day, although coach Jesse Minter did say on Monday that the former MVP could "potentially" return to practice this week . He has yet to take the practice field since spraining his left ankle in a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. If Jackson can't go on Sunday against the Bengals , backup Tyler Huntley will make his third consecutive start. QB Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Bucs are stil preparing for rookie Jalon Daniels to start this Sunday at Carolina. But the ever-insistent Mayfield did take part in Wednesday's practice session while wearing a glove to protect the injured thumb on his passing hand. The big question is whether Mayfield will be able to hold the football securely under game conditions. RB Saquon Barkley, Philadelphia Eagles No news is ... good news? Barkley has missed back-to-back games with a hamstring injury, but there's been no update from the team on his progress so far this week. Dameon Pierce got all the running back carries in Week 6 so he would be the primary ballcarrier again if Barkley can't suit up. He was scheduled to do some running on Tuesday and then take part in practice the following day. Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier have been splitting the backfield duties in Love's absence, with only limited success. Roschon Johnson, who had 85 total yards and a TD vs. the Atlanta Falcons, would once again be the primary backup to D'Andre Swift. WR A.J. item.title: Takeaways From Knicks’ 106-100 Defeat vs 76ers Including Drummond Double-Double
item.description: Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) fights for position against New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby (8) during the first quarter at Madison Square Garden. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik On Tuesday night, New York Knicks players, coaches, and front office members received their championship rings before a sold-out Madison Square Garden watched the 2025-26 World Champions banner rise to the rafters. However, there was still a game to be played afterwards. Following the pomp and circumstance, the Knicks fell to the new-look Philadelphia 76ers by a score of 106-100. Here are some important takeaways from last night’s loss. Takeaways from the Knicks’ Opening Night Loss Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby (8) loses control of the ball during the first quarter against the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images 1. OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges Need to Be Better The first Knicks basket of the game was scored by Mikal Bridges . He got one more basket in the first quarter and was essentially invisible the rest of the game. Bridges finished the game with four points (on 2-of-8 from the field and 0-of-2 from three), three rebounds, one assist, and one block without recording a turnover. In his 33 minutes, he finished with a plus/minus of -15. Last night was not the version of Mikal Bridges that helped win New York a championship. Similar could be said about OG Anunoby . The hero of last year’s Game Four of the Finals played far from that version of himself last night. Anunoby put up an inefficient 10 points on 3-of-12 shooting and was an abysmal 1-of-9 from beyond the arc. He also finished with five rebounds, no assists, two turnovers, a block, and a steal. Anunoby finished with the worst plus/minus of the game with a -20. Anunoby had high expectations coming into this season, and he straight-up failed to meet said expectations last night. Like Bridges, the Knicks have little chance of repeating with these kinds of performances. 2. Andre Drummond Is a Legit Backup Center After losing Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics in free agency, the backup center position was a big topic of discussion throughout the summer. The signing of Andre Drummond to fill the role left some asking questions, while others felt confident in the move. Drummond was needed very quickly in this game as Karl-Anthony Towns got into foul trouble early. His impact on the game was felt quickly too, as he posted a double-double by the end of the first half, scoring 10 points and racking up 12 rebounds in the half. However, due to his increased playing time in the first half, his impact was just not felt nearly as much during his minutes in the second half. Drummond only scored two points and recorded two rebounds in his more limited second-half minutes. It’s hard to imagine he plays the 24 minutes he played in the opener very often, so it isn’t t
item.content:encoded: Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) fights for position against New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby (8) during the first quarter at Madison Square Garden. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik On Tuesday night, New York Knicks players, coaches, and front office members received their championship rings before a sold-out Madison Square Garden watched the 2025-26 World Champions banner rise to the rafters. However, there was still a game to be played afterwards. Following the pomp and circumstance, the Knicks fell to the new-look Philadelphia 76ers by a score of 106-100. Here are some important takeaways from last night’s loss. Takeaways from the Knicks’ Opening Night Loss Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby (8) loses control of the ball during the first quarter against the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images 1. OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges Need to Be Better The first Knicks basket of the game was scored by Mikal Bridges . He got one more basket in the first quarter and was essentially invisible the rest of the game. In his 33 minutes, he finished with a plus/minus of -15. Last night was not the version of Mikal Bridges that helped win New York a championship. Similar could be said about OG Anunoby . The hero of last year’s Game Four of the Finals played far from that version of himself last night. Anunoby put up an inefficient 10 points on 3-of-12 shooting and was an abysmal 1-of-9 from beyond the arc. He also finished with five rebounds, no assists, two turnovers, a block, and a steal. Anunoby finished with the worst plus/minus of the game with a -20. Anunoby had high expectations coming into this season, and he straight-up failed to meet said expectations last night. Like Bridges, the Knicks have little chance of repeating with these kinds of performances. 2. Andre Drummond Is a Legit Backup Center After losing Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics in free agency, the backup center position was a big topic of discussion throughout the summer. The signing of Andre Drummond to fill the role left some asking questions, while others felt confident in the move. Drummond was needed very quickly in this game as Karl-Anthony Towns got into foul trouble early. His impact on the game was felt quickly too, as he posted a double-double by the end of the first half, scoring 10 points and racking up 12 rebounds in the half. However, due to his increased playing time in the first half, his impact was just not felt nearly as much during his minutes in the second half. Drummond only scored two points and recorded two rebounds in his more limited second-half minutes. It’s hard to imagine he plays the 24 minutes he played in the opener very often, so it isn’t too concerning that his production took a dip as he stayed in the game longer. However, when these situations do arise, it may be smart to give James Wiseman some game time to really maximize Drummond’s minutes in the way the Knicks were able to in the first half. The Last Word The Knicks came out flat against a clear contender in Philadelphia. Head coach Mike Brown said that they “looked like [they] were running in mud” during his postgame press conference, which is a very apt description. They were sloppy with the ball, lethargic in transition, and were inefficient from the field with their 37% shooting. This game was clearly not up to the Knicks’ standards, and will never be a good enough effort to beat a strong 76ers team. There will be more marquee Knicks-Sixers matchups in the regular season, and potentially more come playoff time. Philadelphia punched the champions in the mouth, and the Knicks will have to bounce back in Boston on Friday. item.title: Luka Doncic reveals where he wants to finish his NBA career
item.description: Luka Doncic reveals where he wants to finish his NBA career originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . If it's up to Luka Doncic, he'll be in Los Angeles for a long time. Ahead of Wednesday's 2026-27 season opener, the six-time All-Star was asked if he wants to retire as a member of the Los Angeles Lakers . His response was encouraging for Lakers fans. “Hopefully, yeah,” Doncic told the California Post's Melissa Rohlin . There was, however, a catch. “But as you know in this NBA business, you never know what’s going to happen. But I feel like I’ve found something here that’s very comfortable for me. And hopefully [that happens].” MORE: Draymond Green boldly predicts Luka Doncic's future with the NBA MVP award Doncic was traded from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers in a shocking 2025 NBA trade deadline deal. The 2026-27 season will be his second full season in Los Angeles. The team Doncic joined is very different from the one around him now. Not only is LeBron James no longer on the roster, but the Lakers made a number of offseason additions with Doncic specifically in mind. Whether the Lakers like it or not, Doncic's future in L.A. will become a topic sooner rather than later. He's under contract through the 2028-29 season, although the final season is a $57.4 million player option. That means Doncic would become a free agent after the 2027-28 season if he declines his option. For now, at least, Doncic sounds comfortable in Los Angeles. Whether that leads to him finishing his career in a Lakers uniform remains to be seen. item.title: Maybe It Is Time To Overreact
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 20: John Blackwell #13 of the Duke Blue Devils dunks the ball in the second half against the Tennessee Volunteers at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 20, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every Duke preseason follows a familiar routine. During the summer, fans overanalyze every little scrap of intel or footage from early practices. Come the fall, the chatter becomes louder and the excitement builds, cluminating in a lofty pre-season poll ranking. By the time the team finally hits the floor against a real opponent in the exhibition season, the pent up energy of six months without Duke Basketball makes every fan prone to overreact to those first real glimpses of the squad. Overreacting to an exhibition result almost always is a mistake. Last night was the “almost.” It’s hard to overstate how dominant the Blue Devils looked in their dismantling of Tennessee. Six different Duke players scored before Tennessee exceeded six total points. 12 minutes into the game, the Blue Devils had tripled up the visiting Volunteers. For the game, Duke shot 20% better from the field than Tennessee. Statistic after statistic shows pure and utter domination. Yes, this was still an exhibition and Tennessee was not at full strength (although notably neither was Duke without Caleb Foster and Drew Scharnowski). That would be important context if this was a tighter contest. But that possibility was essentially out the window 10 minutes into the game. The fact is that Tennessee came into Cameron Indoor Stadium wanting to win a game in the greatest arena in the sport. And they were humiliated. Strangely, the best analogue for this performance is not any of the contemporary, televised exhibitions against Division I opponents. It is, instead, Mike Krzyzewski’s old tradition of inviting the reigning Division II National Champion for an exhibition contest each year. The question in those contests was never whether Duke would win, but by how much and how good they’d look doing it. There were many years in which the Blue Devils would come out sluggish and not defeat an inferior opponent with the efficiency fans would expect. A 40 point victory—a margin that could have been higher were it not for significant minutes for the deep bench—would be seen as a exciting sign for the season to come. But this wasn’t a DII opponent. It was a pre-season Top 10 Tennessee team coached by Rick Barnes. This is officially the exception to the “don’t overreact to exhibitions” rule. A Top 10 team, even injury-riddled and on the road, is never supposed to lose by nearly 40 points. A squad full of established college basketball players, making up arguably the best collective class of incoming transfers in the country, is not supposed to be embarrassed to this degree. item.content:encoded: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 20: John Blackwell #13 of the Duke Blue Devils dunks the ball in the second half against the Tennessee Volunteers at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 20, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every Duke preseason follows a familiar routine. During the summer, fans overanalyze every little scrap of intel or footage from early practices. For the game, Duke shot 20% better from the field than Tennessee. Statistic after statistic shows pure and utter domination. Yes, this was still an exhibition and Tennessee was not at full strength (although notably neither was Duke without Caleb Foster and Drew Scharnowski). That would be important context if this was a tighter contest. But that possibility was essentially out the window 10 minutes into the game. The fact is that Tennessee came into Cameron Indoor Stadium wanting to win a game in the greatest arena in the sport. And they were humiliated. Strangely, the best analogue for this performance is not any of the contemporary, televised exhibitions against Division I opponents. It is, instead, Mike Krzyzewski’s old tradition of inviting the reigning Division II National Champion for an exhibition contest each year. The question in those contests was never whether Duke would win, but by how much and how good they’d look doing it. There were many years in which the Blue Devils would come out sluggish and not defeat an inferior opponent with the efficiency fans would expect. A 40 point victory—a margin that could have been higher were it not for significant minutes for the deep bench—would be seen as a exciting sign for the season to come. But this wasn’t a DII opponent. It was a pre-season Top 10 Tennessee team coached by Rick Barnes. This is officially the exception to the “don’t overreact to exhibitions” rule. A Top 10 team, even injury-riddled and on the road, is never supposed to lose by nearly 40 points. A squad full of established college basketball players, making up arguably the best collective class of incoming transfers in the country, is not supposed to be embarrassed to this degree. Even if they haven’t yet formed a cohesive unit and aren’t fully deserving of that lofty Top 10 ranking, there was not a DI vs DII discrepancy in talent, athleticism, and size on the floor in Cameron last night. Yet, it looks that way in the boxscore. Time to get excited, Duke fans. Time to get excited about John Blackwell, who appears to have adjusted from his high-volume role at Wisconsin into an ultra-efficient scorer as a Blue Devil. Time to get excited by Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje, who at 17 years old outclassed opponents many years his senior. Time to get excited by the fact that Duke’s projected fourth guard, freshman Derron Rippey Jr., was the best player on the court in a Top 10 matchup for significant stretches. Time to get excited by the major leaps forward that returnees Dame Sarr and Patrick Ngongba II have made. By the way: maybe find some space to recognize this Duke team is shooting 87.5% from the FT line through two exhibition contests. But you can be forgiven for overlooking a subplot like that amidst all this excitement. Go to the DBR Boards to find Blue Healer Auctions || Drop us a line

item.title: Week 7 Fantasy Football Running Back Streamers: Zach Charbonnet, Mike Washington Jr, And More Streaming Options
item.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet (26) rushes the ball against the San Francisco 49ers during the first half at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In a perfect world, we would all have a superstar to plug into every spot in our fantasy football lineups. Unfortunately, that is rarely the case, especially as we get deeper into the season. We all have to adjust to bye weeks, injuries, and tough matchups. One of the toughest and most important positions to get right from week to week is running backs. That's why we are here to help you find some desperation options who could have a solid week. These are our top fantasy football running back streamers for Week 7. RB Brian Robinson Jr, Atlanta Falcons We haven't seen much out of Robinson in the past few weeks, but we know he has a shot at finding the end zone in that backfield. He has scored four touchdowns this season and, in his first four games of the season, carried the ball 44 times for 194 yards. The Falcons are going to have to get back to their run-dominant approach after dropping their last two games. We expect them to do that this week in an above-average matchup against a banged-up San Francisco 49ers defense. RB Mike Washington Jr, Las Vegas Raiders Ashton Jeanty is clearly not healthy, and Washington is getting more opportunities. In Week 6, Washington saw nine carries to Jeanty's 10 and was much more efficient. Washington rushed for 43 yards at 4.8 yards per carry, while Jeanty turned his 10 carries into just 22 yards at 2.2 yards per carry. We wouldn't be surprised if that continues this week or if Jeanty ends up missing the game completely, much like what we saw with Jeremiyah Love last week in Arizona. If Washington survived your waiver wire this week or is stashed on your bench, you should consider starting him this week if you're scrambling for a running back. RB Zach Charbonnet, Seattle Seahawks Charbonnet is trending towards returning in Week 7. While he could be eased back in coming off a torn ACL in January, he could also step in as the lead back in Seattle. This is exactly the kind of opportunity you look for when streaming a running back. Despite a tough matchup against the Chiefs this week, Charbonnet is an interesting option if he's available on your waiver wire or stashed on your IR. He could realistically see 10 carries, a handful of targets, and handle the goal-line work this week. RB Pierre Strong, Green Bay Packers Josh Jacobs is back this week, and he is going to destroy any minimal value MarShawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson might have had. However, that might not be the case for Strong. With Chris Brooks still on injured reserve, Strong should maintain his role as the change-of-pace and primary pass-catching back. While we expect Jacobs to get more touches, we wouldn't be surprised if Jacobs and Strong have a near-even split of the offensive snaps in Jacobs' first week back. More Fantasy Sports On S

RB Pierre Strong, Green Bay Packers Josh Jacobs is back this week, and he is going to destroy any minimal value MarShawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson might have had. However, that might not be the case for Strong. With Chris Brooks still on injured reserve, Strong should maintain his role as the change-of-pace and primary pass-catching back. While we expect Jacobs to get more touches, we wouldn't be surprised if Jacobs and Strong have a near-even split of the offensive snaps in Jacobs' first week back. item.title: Royal County Down Submit Plans For Upgrades To Its Championship Course
item.description: NEWCASTLE, NORTHERN IRELAND - SEPTEMBER 10: A general view of the first green as players putt during a practice round prior to the Amgen Irish Open 2024 at Royal County Down Golf Club on September 10, 2024 in Newcastle, Northern Ireland. (Photo by Ross Kinnaird/Getty Images) Getty Images Royal County Down Golf Club, whose championship course is one of the world’s most revered golf courses, stated that they are preparing for work to be done on the Championship course. Royal County Down, which is located in Northern Ireland, consistently ranks as one of the most scenic, and also one of the toughest, golf courses in the world. In fact, has been rated as number one in the World’s 100 greatest and number one in the Best in the United Kingdom and Ireland categories by Golf Digest . It therefore comes as a surprise that Royal County Down Golf Club has announced plans for changes to both their Championship and Annesley courses. In a planning statement submitted by the club , the goal is to “significantly upgrade the course to reflect RCD’s status as one of the very best golf courses in the world and one of the most significant golf tourism assets in Northern Ireland”. Royal County Down has never hosted an Open Championship, and the work could be an attempt to attract an Open Championship in the future. It would make sense then that architecture firm Mackenzie & Ebert was chosen to carry out the work. Mackenzie & Ebert have experience working on Open Championship Rota courses, having done work on eight of the ten venues including Royal Lytham and St Annes, Royal St. George’s, Royal Troon, Royal Liverpool, Royal Birkdale, Carnoustie, Turnberry, and Royal Portrush. Changes proposed by Mackenzie & Ebert include adjustments to existing tee boxes, new teeing grounds, a new green on the 5th hole, as well as reshaping and remodeling of the closing stretch of holes, 16-18. Changes are also proposed for holes 1, 3, 5, 11, and 12. While the planning statement references upgrades to the course to maintain its status quo atop the golf course rankings, it does not specifically state a desire to host an Open Championship. Rather, the statement goes on to say the works will help the club to “continue to attract and support the hosting of large events, building upon the success of the hosting of the Amgen Irish Open in 2024”. While around 70,000 visited Royal County Down during the Amgen Irish Open in 2024, attendance was capped at 16,000 per day. Contrast those numbers with the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, which hosted 306,000 fans. While plans have been submitted, they are subject to approval by the planning committee in the district council. If approved, work could begin in 2027. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: NFL world reacts to conflicting statements from NFL medical exec, NFLPA on Jalen Hurts situation
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Eagles have faced widespread scrutiny for their handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts’ health over the past two weeks. The franchise announced ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers that Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. Then, news broke on Monday that Hurts would miss the rest of the season after further tests revealed several blood clots in his lungs. The week before, he’d been cleared to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London despite having already been diagnosed with blood clots in his calf and advised not to sleep, and also took an international flight home from London with the active blood clots. The Eagles’ handling of Hurts’ health has since been widely questioned, with CBS’ Leger Douzable going as far as to characterize it as “disturbing.” Still, the NFL told The Athletic that the process surrounding the quarterback was “handled appropriately,” and in response to the backlash, NFL Chief Medical Officer Allen Sills spent nearly five minutes on Tuesday defending Philadelphia’s protocol to reporters, asserting that reports insinuating that any of the league’s physicians would put a player in harm’s way are “nonsense.” NFL Chief Medical Officer Allen Sills gave a nearly 5-minute defense of the league and Eagles protocol in treating Jalen Hurts’ blood clots. Called some reports “nonsense” and insisted that no doctors are taking orders from football coaches or management when treating patients. https://t.co/LvmzoYvPYy — Jori Epstein (@JoriEpstein) October 20, 2026 The NFLPA, however, released a statement Tuesday evening stating that the league made it clear it hadn’t investigated the protocol the Eagles followed, and had no intention of doing so before calling for a full investigation: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” Media members on social media had a wide range of reactions to the NFLPA’s statement and Sills’ address. The NFL wasn’t really telling the truth. I’m SHOCKED. — Jemele Hill (@jemelehill) October 21, 2026 On his Night Cap podcast, Shannon Sharpe expressed gratitude for the NFL and how it changed his family’s life before calling the league out for its willingness to cover up health concerns, which he said he’d experienced himself. His co-host, Chad Ochocinco, asserted that team doctors always act in what’s best for the team rather than the players, even if it’s intentionally misdiagnosing injuries to ensure that key players are available to play. item.title: Senate rejects NMDPRA’s PMS import records, summons agency heads
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Public Accounts has rejected the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL). The committee, chaired by Senator Ahmed Wadada Dankwambo, resolved on Wednesday to summon the heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) to explain the discrepancies and reconcile the conflicting records. The decision followed the NMDPRA’s response to queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023. Appearing before the committee, the NMDPRA’s Authority Chief Executive, Mallam Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, was represented by Deputy Director Uzoamaka Ugwu-Ojobe, who maintained that the authority’s records were credible despite the differences. She told the committee that NMDPRA recorded 3.29 billion litres of PMS imports in 2022 and 6.02 billion litres in 2023, compared with the 6.27 billion litres and 3.88 billion litres reported by NNPCL for the respective years. “The slight disparities are being looked into for possible reconciliation,” she said. However, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, rejected the description of the differences as slight, noting that the figures showed substantial variations that required serious investigation. “The disparities in records of PMS importation between NMDPRA and NNPCL in 2022 and 2023, as stated in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report of 2021 to 2023, are too wide to be described as slight or being looked into without the seriousness required,” he said. Similarly, Senator Dayo Faduyile, representing Ondo South, said the discrepancies raised concerns about the reliability of the records submitted by the two agencies. He said the differences left room for questions about what might have gone wrong in the reporting of petroleum imports. Senator Anietan Bassey, representing Akwa Ibom North-East, called for a thorough investigation, insisting that Nigerians must not be shortchanged because of discrepancies in official records. “Mr Chairman and very distinguished colleagues, these questionable records of volume of PMS importation by the two agencies must be thoroughly investigated to save Nigerians from being yearly shortchanged and expose those milking the country dry,” he said. In his remarks, Dankwambo said the committee would convene a meeting involving the three agencies to establish the reasons for the conflicting figures. “In view of the unacceptability of presentations made by the representative of NMDPRA on queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023, specifically on volume of PMS imported within the years under review, this committee resolved to summon heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and NEITI for reasons behind the wide dis

item.title: AI will eat a fifth of tech budgets in 2027, but don't expect it to pay for itself
item.description: More than half of CIOs are likely to miss their AI-related ROI targets next year, according to Forrester. The analyst's State Of AI Survey 2026 found that 45 percent of AI decision-makers need positive ROI within a year to consider their investments successful. Some tech leaders will get better at tying AI spend to planned returns. However, Forrester expects success to be confined to isolated use cases rather than whole programs, which won't be enough. “As with prior emerging technologies, organizational structures, processes, and ways of working need to change to drive measurable, firmwide results with AI,” the report says. Only 22 percent of AI decision-makers report a positive AI impact on EBITDA (earnings before income tax, depreciation and amortization) over the past 12 months. “This mismatch between the investment into technology adoption and organizational change will delay the realization of heightened ROI targets,” the report adds. The money will keep flowing through IT budgets regardless. In its Technology & Security Predictions, Forrester claimed AI will account for 20 percent of all business technology spend next year. Sharyn Leaver, chief research officer at Forrester, said that will increase the pressure on leaders to prove AI's value while keeping costs, infrastructure, and risk under control. “At the same time, emerging technologies, geopolitical pressures, and the growing use of AI across technology operations will introduce new complexities and potential points of failure,” she said. While tech teams struggle to get returns from growing AI spending, they will try to get more bang for their buck by investing in open-weight GenAI models, which can approach similar performance to the leading proprietary systems, at a fraction of the cost. Open-weight models will represent half of AI tokens but only five percent of enterprise spend, Forrester predicts. “Open-weight models such as Gemma, Llama, or Qwen are good enough for the enterprise workloads that generate the most token volume, such as document processing, customer support conversations, internal knowledge search, and the routine substeps inside agentic workflows,” Forrester said. Frontier models, including Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, and Google's Gemini 4 Argon, will be reserved for “the few deep knowledge and critical task automations where errors are expensive, but the token count will tip toward open weight”, Forrester said.

item.title: Boban slams Bruno Fernandes: ‘United won’t have a strong future if he’s the best player’
item.description: Boban slams Bruno Fernandes: ‘United won’t have a strong future if he’s the best player’ It’s safe to say that former Milan midfielder and Sky Sport Italia pundit Zvonimir Boban is not a fan of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, claiming that the Premier League side ‘will not have a present or future at a strong level as long as he is the best player’. Fernandes was named in the Manchester United starting line-up for their visit to the Stadio Sinigaglia to take on Como in the Champions League league phase on Wednesday evening. You can follow the action from Wednesday’s Champions League matches on the Football Italia Liveblog. Boban critisicm of Bruno Fernandes ahead of Como vs. Manchester United ZAGREB, CROATIA – OCTOBER 25: Former footballer Zvonimir Boban looks on prior to kick off of the UEFA Champions League group E match between Dinamo Zagreb and AC Milan at Stadion Maksimir on October 25, 2022 in Zagreb, Croatia. (Photo by Jurij Kodrun/Getty Images) Boban was among the pundits in the studio for Sky Sport Italia’s coverage of the Como vs. Manchester United match and was asked for his thoughts on United’s captain and star player, Bruno Fernandes. The Portugal international spent five years in Italy at the beginning of his career with stints at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria, before moving to Sporting CP in 2017. Boban feels that the United captain is a ‘good player’ but feels that they will not be able to compete at the highest levels ‘as long as he is the best player’. LEEDS, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 18: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United in action during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road on October 18, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Bruno Fernandes is a good player, but they are acting as if he’s a top star, and he does not belong at that level of football,” Boban told Sky Sport Italia. “As long as he is the best player at Manchester United, then Manchester United will not have a present or future at a strong level. We are talking about a perfectly good player, he understands football, moves in spaces, reads it well, but he is a very long way off the level of what ought to be a leader at a club like Manchester United.”

item.title: Another Star May Have Re-Signed With WWE
item.description: WWE Ivy Nile may have quietly signed a new deal with WWE. According to Fightful Select , Nile’s contract was due to expire at the beginning of October. However, she is still listed as an active talent on WWE’s roster page, and she appeared on the October 6 episode of NXT in a battle royal to determine the number one contender for the NXT Women’s Championship. That match was won by Wren Sinclair, who was impersonating Lady Shani. Her NXT appearance came after a long stretch away from WWE’s main shows. Nile has been off Raw since March, and she has wrestled only two matches on the show this year. Most of her work in 2026 has come on WWE Main Event, where she has wrestled 12 times, including matches against NXT talent such as Thea Hail, Wendy Choo and Lizzy Rain. Fightful Select reported in early September that Nile’s contract was set to expire soon and that it had not heard whether she had negotiated a new deal. The same report said WWE had plans for her and that creative had a “big change” in store. Fightful Select later reported that the change was a tag team with Jordynne Grace. According to Fightful, vignettes pairing the two were filmed over the summer, with the hope that they would air in September, and its sources linked the team to the WWE trademark “Iron Built.” The vignettes never aired. In May 2025, she won the tournament to become number one contender for the WWE Women’s Speed Championship but lost to Sol Ruca in the title match. Grace has also been off television, and a WrestleVotes report said WWE does not have her in its creative plans at the moment, while adding that she is not on her way out. What Ivy Nile’s WWE Contract Status Means Nile still being on the roster is a good sign that the company sees value in her, even after a year in which she was barely used on Raw. Her name staying on the roster page and her appearance on NXT television right after her contract was due to expire both point to her still being under contract, and they suggest the company wants her visible again. The Grace team is still the best path for her. Both women have strength-based styles and are competing in bodybuilding, the vignettes are already filmed, and the women’s tag team division needs new challengers. Tatum Paxley holding the tag titles with Alexa Bliss also gives Nile a built-in story against her former partner. The concern is that WWE has had this plan ready since the summer and still has not pulled the trigger. If Nile did sign a new deal, the company should use it as a reason to finally air those vignettes and give both women something to do on television. Related Headlines Chad Gable Is Quietly Having a Huge Title Run WWE Hall of Famer Kevin Nash Reveals Recent Health Concerns: ‘I Thought My Life Was Going to Crash and Burn’ New Rumor Claims Dragon Lee Has Inked New WWE Contract: Is a Big Push Coming Next? Grace has also been off television, and a WrestleVotes report said WWE does not have her in its creative plans at the moment, while adding that she is not on her way out. What Ivy Nile’s WWE Contract Status Means Nile still being on the roster is a good sign that the company sees value in her, even after a year in which she was barely used on Raw. Her name staying on the roster page and her appearance on NXT television right after her contract was due to expire both point to her still being under contract, and they suggest the company wants her visible again. The Grace team is still the best path for her. Both women have strength-based styles and are competing in bodybuilding, the vignettes are already filmed, and the women’s tag team division needs new challengers. Tatum Paxley holding the tag titles with Alexa Bliss also gives Nile a built-in story against her former partner. The concern is that WWE has had this plan ready since the summer and still has not pulled the trigger. If Nile did sign a new deal, the company should use it as a reason to finally air those vignettes and give both women something to do on television. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to face the Super Bowl runner-up New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football. The Patriots started the season slowly, just 1-2, with losses to Jacksonville and Seattle. Drake Maye was playing bad football, too. He led the league in interceptions with six in the first three games. But they’ve turned a corner. Maye is playing much better and they come to Chicago riding a three-game winning streak. They upset the Bills, blew out the feisty, upstart Raiders and took care of the Jets. This game creates a test of sorts for the Patriots. Are they the team that beat the Bills and took out the Raiders, Jets and Steelers? Or are they the team that lost to the Seahawks with a back-breaking interception and got trounced by the Jaguars? For Chicago, it’s a step up in competition. They have also been rocky — with comfortable wins over the Panthers and Jets — but ugly losses to the Packers and Vikings. And just last week they did their best to cough up a 31-7 lead in their 31-23 win over the Falcons. But as usual, there are plenty of reasons for those blips. Backup QBs, bad weather and in the case of the Falcons, inserting backup players too soon in a game they led comfortably. Each of these teams wants to establish themselves as a true contender and be mentioned above the best teams in the league. A Thursday night win on national streaming TV could go a long way. Plus, it’s a rematch for two of the top 3 overall picks of the 2024 NFL Draft with Caleb Williams and Drake Maye. It’s sure to be brought up, as well as when they faced off as rookies. That game did not go Caleb’s way. item.content:encoded: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots drops back to pass during the second half during the NFL game against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to face the Super Bowl runner-up New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football. The Patriots started the season slowly, just 1-2, with losses to Jacksonville and Seattle. Drake Maye was playing bad football, too. He led the league in interceptions with six in the first three games. But they’ve turned a corner. Maye is playing much better and they come to Chicago riding a three-game winning streak. They upset the Bills, blew out the feisty, upstart Raiders and took care of the Jets. This game creates a test of sorts for the Patriots. Are they the team that beat the Bills and took out the Raiders, Jets and Steelers? Or are they the team that lost to the Seahawks with a back-breaking interception and got trounced by the Jaguars? For Chicago, it’s a step up in competition. They have also been rocky — with comfortable wins over the Panthers and Jets — but ugly losses to the Packers and Vikings. And just last week they did their best to cough up a 31-7 lead in their 31-23 win over the Falcons. But as usual, there are plenty of reasons for those blips. Backup QBs, bad weather and in the case of the Falcons, inserting backup players too soon in a game they led comfortably. Each of these teams wants to establish themselves as a true contender and be mentioned above the best teams in the league. A Thursday night win on national streaming TV could go a long way. Plus, it’s a rematch for two of the top 3 overall picks of the 2024 NFL Draft with Caleb Williams and Drake Maye. It’s sure to be brought up, as well as when they faced off as rookies. That game did not go Caleb’s way. New England Patriots SB Nation site: Pats Pulpit Record: 4-2, 2nd in the AFC East Last week: 26-19 win over the Jets Game day, time, TV: Thursday, 7:15 p.m., Amazon Prime Video Spread: Bears -2.5 Bears all-time record against: 5-11, including postseason (Super Bowl XX that is!) Historical meetings: In week 7 of the 2022 season, Matt Eberflus and the Bears went to New England to face the Patriots on Monday Night Football. Mac Jones was benched after starting 3 for 6 for 13 yards and an interception to Jaquan Brisker. Bailey Zappe didn’t fare much better and was picked by Roquan Smith and Kyler Gordon. Justin Fields and David Montgomery rushed for touchdowns. Fields threw another TD to Khalil Herbert and the Bears won 33-14. It was their last win of the 2022 season Last meeting: Week 10 of the 2024 season. The Bears hosted the Patriots in a game to forget. The Patriots were 2-7, and the Bears laid a total egg. Four Joey Slye field goals and a Ja’Lynn Polk TD from Drake Maye were all the Pats needed to win 19-3. Caleb Williams was sacked nine times, and the Bears mustered only 142 total yards. Patriots won 19-3. Injury report: Eight Patriots were listed on their Tuesday estimated injury report. Did not participate C Ben Brown (knee) CB Carlton Davis III (neck) DT Joshua Farmer (personal) Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) Limited participation WR A.J. Brown (ankle) CB Channing Canada (hamstring) T Morgan Moses (foot) CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) Offense: The Patriots offense enters this week ranked 18th in points but seventh in yards. They are 10th in passing yards and sixth in rushing yards. Drake Maye (63.9 pct cmp./1,463 yds./11 TD/7 INT) rebounded from a rough early couple of games to return to the form he showed last year. Since starting the year with one touchdown and six interceptions over the first three games, he has 10 TDs to just one INT in the last three. With A.J. Brown (6 rec./53 yds/0 TD) missing time, Maye is relying on WR Demario Douglas (20/233/3), TE Hunter Henry (19/225/2 TD), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (15/111/0) and Mack Hollins (15/209/0). Former Packer Romeo Doubs (14/261/3) is the main deep threat. Eli Raridon (9/112/1), Efton Chism III (9/98/1) and Kyle Williams (6/147/1) each have touchdowns, too. On the ground, it’s mostly Stevenson (71 att./263 yds./2 TD), followed by TreVeyon Henderson (49/194/1). Maye (34/185/1) makes some runs, too. Corey Kiner (31/138/0) also gets worked in. Defense: The Patriots enter the week fifth in points allowed and sixth in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks 11th and their rushing defense ranks ninth. Christian Gonzalez (14 tkls/5 PD/0 INT) became the highest-paid CB this summer and is a true No. 1 corner. With him, Marcus Jones (1 INT/5 PD/27 tkl), Charles Woods (25 tkls/5 PD/1 INT) and our old friend Kevin Byard (26 tkls/2 PD/0 INT) are patrolling the secondary. Craig Woodson (23 tkls/1 FR/2 PD/1 INT) also makes plays. Up front, LBs Robert Spillane (39 tkls/2 QB hits/1 TFL) and Christian Elliss (38 tkls/1 sk/1 TFL/3 QB hits/1 FF/1 PD) lead the Pats in tackles. Elijah Ponder (5.5 sks/7 TFL/10 QB hits/2 FR/1 FF) and Christian Barmore (2 sks/2 TFL/5 QB hits/1 PD) lead the pass rush. Gabe Jacas (1.5 sk/1 INT/1 PD/3 TFL/5 QB hits) and Milton Williams (1 sk/1 TFL/2 QB hits/38 tkls) are also making stops up front. Key matchups: It’ll be interesting to see how Christian Gonzalez is used and how Ben Johnson tries to get his pass-catchers in favorable matchups. Mike Vrabel is a good defensive coordinator, and he’ll throw a lot at Chicago to get the offense off balance and out of sync. Dennis Allen, on the other hand, has to use his disguises and blitzes well against Drake Maye to try and get him looking like the Maye from the Super Bowl and the first three games of the season. Not the Maye from the last three weeks. Key stats The Patriots defense ranks seventh in red zone defense, allowing touchdowns on 50 percent of opponents’ drives. The Bears, after their red zone performance, are scoring on 50 percent of their red zone drives. New England ranks ninth in blitz percentage, sending extra pressure 31.9 percent of the time. However, they rank 13th in pressure percentage, getting pressure 23.9 percent of the time. Chicago ranks fourth in pressure percentage at 30.2 percent. The Pats are allowing the ninth-worst completion percentage to opposing QBs at 66.1 percent. QBs have a 90.3 rating against their defense. New England has the second-most turnovers on offense with 13. Seven interceptions by Maye and six lost fumbles. The Patriots have 11 fumbles on the season and have lost six of them Can the Bears beat the Patriots at home? Which of these teams is the more likely “pretender,” and which one is more likely the “contender?” Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Football Italia Show: Italian TOTW – 3 potential new additions for Mancini
item.description: Football Italia Show: Italian TOTW – 3 potential new additions for Mancini Lorenzo Bettoni and Richard Hall return with a brand-new episode of the Football Italia Show, taking a closer look at the standout Italian performers across Europe’s top five leagues and selecting their Team of the Week. Click here to subscribe to the Official Football Italia YouTube channel Among the players to make the cut are Euro 2020 winners Domenico Berardi and Emerson Palmieri, who continue to make their mark at club level. Italian TOTW in Europe’s top 5 leagues MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Domenico Berardi of Sassuolo in action during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) However, this week’s selection also looks towards the future of the Azzurri, with Mattia Liberali, Emanuele Lulli and Antonio Raimondo emerging as potential new additions to the Italy squad ahead of the next international break. Could any of the three be in contention for a call-up as Italy look to strengthen their options? FROSINONE, ITALY – OCTOBER 16: Antonio Raimondo of Frosinone Calcio celebrates after scoring goal 3-1 during the Serie A match between Frosinone Calcio and US Sassuolo at Stadio Benito Stirpe on October 16, 2026 in Frosinone, Italy. (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images) Watch the full episode of the Football Italia Show to see our picks for the Italian Team of the Week, find out who impressed across Europe’s top five leagues, and hear our thoughts on players who could soon feature for the Azzurri. Let us know in the comments below whether you agree with our choices and who else deserves a place in our XI!
