item.title: Cowboys are getting dangerously close to thinking about the draft
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is a point in every disappointing season when the conversation shifts from how a team can make the playoffs to whether it has any realistic chance of competing at all. After another lifeless start and a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, the Dallas Cowboys are getting dangerously close to that point. At 2-4, with consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay, this team looks less like a playoff contender and more like one that could be picking near the top of the 2027 NFL Draft… if they had that pick. Instead, the New York Jets would likely have it for the Quinnen Williams trade unless the Green Bay Packers fall apart and the one Dallas got in the Micah Parsons trade is even higher up. That is a brutal place to be for a team with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and an offense that entered Week 6 averaging 27.6 points per game. Yet the Cowboys have scored just 29 points combined in their last two games. They were held scoreless in the first half at Lambeau Field for the first time since November 2021, and the offense looked completely out of answers when Green Bay turned up the pressure. Questioning the heart of football players is usually a foolish take. The desire to be a great team, however, doesn’t seem to show up consistently, particularly in the details that separate winning teams from losing ones. The discipline is missing, the adjustments are not translating into better football, and the leaders have not found a way to pull everyone out of this spiral, which feels like it has been going on since the last time the Cowboys made the playoffs in 2023. I wonder who that team lost to? The same mistakes keep showing up Good teams will lose games on the road. The Cowboys faced familiar problems and took extra time to regroup after their defeat in Tampa Bay. On Sunday, Dallas committed 11 penalties for 108 yards against Green Bay, reinforcing a season-long concern about discipline. Penalties extend opposing drives, put the offense behind the chains and erase opportunities for a team that cannot afford to give away free yardage. The defense did show some signs of improvement. Dallas held Green Bay to 57 rushing yards, recorded three sacks and kept the Packers out of the end zone in the second half. Joey Porter Jr. has brought a physical presence to the secondary, and there were stretches when the Cowboys made Jordan Love uncomfortable. But the improvement remains inconsistent, and one of the defense’s biggest problems returned: third-down defense. Green Bay converted 11 of 18 third-down attempts, including nine of its first ten. The Packers repeatedly extended drives that should have ended, controlling the pace of the game and keeping Dallas’ offense on the sideline. On the opening touchdown drive alone, Green Bay converted four third downs, twice overcoming third-and-13. Teams are now converting 50% of 3rd and 9+ attempts against the Cowboys this season
item.content:encoded: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is a point in every disappointing season when the conversation shifts from how a team can make the playoffs to whether it has any realistic chance of competing at all. After another lifeless start and a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, the Dallas Cowboys are getting dangerously close to that point. At 2-4, with consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay, this team looks less like a playoff contender and more like one that could be picking near the top of the 2027 NFL Draft… if they had that pick. Instead, the New York Jets would likely have it for the Quinnen Williams trade unless the Green Bay Packers fall apart and the one Dallas got in the Micah Parsons trade is even higher up. That is a brutal place to be for a team with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and an offense that entered Week 6 averaging 27.6 points per game. Yet the Cowboys have scored just 29 points combined in their last two games. They were held scoreless in the first half at Lambeau Field for the first time since November 2021, and the offense looked completely out of answers when Green Bay turned up the pressure. Questioning the heart of football players is usually a foolish take. The desire to be a great team, however, doesn’t seem to show up consistently, particularly in the details that separate winning teams from losing ones. The discipline is missing, the adjustments are not translating into better football, and the leaders have not found a way to pull everyone out of this spiral, which feels like it has been going on since the last time the Cowboys made the playoffs in 2023. I wonder who that team lost to? The same mistakes keep showing up Good teams will lose games on the road. The Cowboys faced familiar problems and took extra time to regroup after their defeat in Tampa Bay. On Sunday, Dallas committed 11 penalties for 108 yards against Green Bay, reinforcing a season-long concern about discipline. Penalties extend opposing drives, put the offense behind the chains and erase opportunities for a team that cannot afford to give away free yardage. The defense did show some signs of improvement. Dallas held Green Bay to 57 rushing yards, recorded three sacks and kept the Packers out of the end zone in the second half. Joey Porter Jr. has brought a physical presence to the secondary, and there were stretches when the Cowboys made Jordan Love uncomfortable. But the improvement remains inconsistent, and one of the defense’s biggest problems returned: third-down defense. Green Bay converted 11 of 18 third-down attempts, including nine of its first ten. The Packers repeatedly extended drives that should have ended, controlling the pace of the game and keeping Dallas’ offense on the sideline. On the opening touchdown drive alone, Green Bay converted four third downs, twice overcoming third-and-13. Teams are now converting 50% of 3rd and 9+ attempts against the Cowboys this season. League average is 21.8% @1053thefan — Bobby Belt (@BobbyBeltTX) October 19, 2026 That is how a defense can make individual plays and still fail to do its job. A sack or a tackle for loss means little if the opponent converts the next third down and keeps marching toward the end zone. Porter and the rest of the secondary can provide encouraging individual performances, but coverage and pressure must work together. The Cowboys cannot keep asking their defensive backs to hold up indefinitely while opposing offenses convert in the situations that should favor the defense. There is progress to acknowledge, but progress without consistency does not win games. Brian Schottenheimer has to turn accountability into results Brian Schottenheimer and QB Dak Prescott are starting to sound like broken records after taking responsibility for the offense’s shortcomings. Don’t get it twisted; that is the appropriate response from a head coach and a franchise quarterback. Neither should point fingers at teammates or make excuses for another loss. But accepting responsibility is the first step, not the finish line. It seems the Cowboys have been back to square one for a while now. Schottenheimer’s play-calling continues to raise serious questions. Dallas rushed for just 48 yards on 15 carries, while Prescott attempted 54 passes. After Javonte Williams scored the Cowboys’ first touchdown early in the third quarter, Dallas ran the ball only once more. Schottenheimer acknowledged the imbalance wasn’t part of the plan, but that explanation only reinforces the problem: whatever the plan is, the Cowboys aren’t executing it or adapting effectively when the game changes. Brian Schottenheimer is broken pic.twitter.com/I1hQoHGVFi — Zac (@Zac_LeeDM) October 19, 2026 Some of that imbalance stemmed from Dallas falling behind 17-0 at halftime. That’s important to note, but it doesn’t explain the broader offensive struggles, especially since the team had nearly two weeks of preparation between games and still came out flat. Prescott finished with 258 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He was pressured 21 times, and his two first-half interceptions helped Green Bay build its lead. The offensive line struggled to protect him; the running game never established itself, and the play-calling failed to provide a consistent answer against Green Bay’s pressure. That fourth-down throw late in the game was another painful example. Facing a fourth-and-11 at the Packers’ 14-yard line, Prescott heaved the ball toward the end zone under heavy pressure, but the pass sailed out of bounds. The situation was desperate, and the pressure was real, but the play ended without giving his receivers a realistic chance to make a play. dak prescott throws it out on 4th down pic.twitter.com/sFUtVM3uhY — wok (@wokdior) October 19, 2026 Prescott does not deserve all the blame for the loss. He was under pressure much of the night, and the offense around him wasn’t good enough. Still, franchise quarterbacks are expected to lead when things get difficult. That means making better decisions, helping the offense settle down and finding ways to keep the team alive when the game is slipping away. The same standard applies to Schottenheimer. A coach can own the mistakes after a loss, but if the same mistakes keep happening, accountability starts to ring hollow. Dallas has heard the explanations. Now it needs to see meaningful changes in the game plan, the execution and the results. This team cannot get all three phases right at the same time The most frustrating part of the Cowboys’ season thus far is how rarely the pieces seem to work together. When the offense is producing, the defense has struggled to stop anybody. When the defense shows signs of life, the offense disappears. Against Green Bay, Dallas’ defense improved after halftime, allowing just six points and generating pressure, but the offense could not capitalize on the opportunity to make the game competitive. The first half was the clearest illustration. Dallas failed to score, Prescott threw two interceptions, and Green Bay built a 17-0 lead. The Cowboys had opportunities to change the momentum, including a defensive interception by linebacker Dee Winters, but the offense immediately gave the ball back, in the red zone no less. It was Dallas’ first interception of the season, a welcome development that nevertheless came amid another frustrating night for the team as a whole. Even the late touchdown did little to change the overall picture. Ryan Flournoy’s six-yard score cut the deficit to 10 points with less than a minute remaining, but the Cowboys failed on the two-point conversion. By then, too many possessions had been wasted and too many mistakes had accumulated. The game had been long over. Green Bay wasn’t flawless, but the Packers made the plays that mattered, and Dallas didn’t. That is the difference between a team that can recover from a rough stretch and one that ke

item.title: Declan Rice touts Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane as best he’s ever played with
item.description: Declan Rice has shared a significant endorsement of Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, naming the England captain as the best player he has ever played alongside. Asked by Viaplay to name the best player he has ever played with, the Arsenal midfielder didn’t hesitate. “Harry Kane, for sure,” Rice said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). The two England internationals have shared the pitch for their country, giving Rice a firsthand look at what Kane brings to the table. While Rice has pl ayed alongside plenty of elite talent at club and international level, it is Kane who apparently stands above the rest. For Bayern Munich fans, th at answer should come as little surprise. Kane has been a phenomenal addition since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur, combining his world-class finishing with e xceptional link-up play, intelligent movement, and an ability to create chances for his teammates. He is far more than a traditional No. 9, and his influence extends well beyond the goals he scores. Rice has also experienced Kane’s quality in the England setup, whe re the striker has been a central figure for years. Playing alongside someone of Kane’s caliber can give even the best midfie lders a different level of confidence, knowing that one pass or one moment of quality can change a game . Of course, Rice will be hoping Kane’s brilliance takes a back seat when Bayern and Arsenal face off. The Gunners midfielder knows e xactly what the England captain can do, and Bayern will be counting on their No. 9 to deliver agains t one of Europe’s strongest sides. When a player of Rice’s quality names Kane as the best he has ever played with, it says plenty ab out the level Bayern Munich have leading their attack. Join the conversation! item.title: The staggering distance Kyle Berkshire has just driven the ball to break his own world record
item.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Kyle Berkshire is well known as the longest hitter of the golf ball on the planet. Berkshire won the World Long Drive Championship four times during a five-year period from 2019 to 2023. The 6ft 3in powerhouse generates tremendous speed and has been known to exceed 230 mph ball speeds with the driver. Kyle Berkshire holds numerous records already including the longest drive on a golf course and the longest drive on a runway – 1,060 yards for what it’s worth! Berkshire’s world record long drive on a golf course stood at 579 yards before this week. The 29-year-old set that record in 2023 after clocking a 241.6 mph ball speed with his driver. And now he has beaten that record without reaching a ball speed as high as the one he generated three years ago. The staggering distance Kyle Berkshire just drove the ball to break his own world record Berkshire attempted to beat his world record this week in Rawlins, Wyoming. The long-drive legend posted a video of his attempts to beat his own record to his official YouTube account. The American powerhouse did not let anyone down. He produced an absolute monster of a drive after clocking a 234.2 ball speed. With that swing, he recorded a drive that travelled a total distance of 588.3 yards – an absolutely gargantuan hit. It is worth pointing out that Berkshire’s drive was downhill and downwind, although he only got 48 yards of run. Berkshire carried his ball an incredible 540 yards through the air. If only Kyle Berkshire was able to tone down his speed and was even half decent from 100 yards and in, he would surely be a real force on the PGA Tour. That said, there is plenty of money in online content creation these days, so it might not even be worth his time trying to sharpen up his game in order to compete on professional tours.

That said, there is plenty of money in online content creation these days, so it might not even be worth his time trying to sharpen up his game in order to compete on professional tours.

item.title: Ian Rapoport’s Josh Jacobs update indicates expected Week 7 Packers status
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Ian Rapoport’s Josh Jacobs update indicates expected Week 7 Packers status appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs being taken off the commissioner’s exempt list, the player is looking to return to the team after a battery case involving a former girlfriend. As the Packers take on the Detroit Lions in Week 7, this NFL insider gives the latest on Jacobs’ status for the contest. While speculation continues on the NFL suspending Jacobs, he is currently eligible to play in Sunday’s game and is on track to do so as well, as the 28-year-old has returned to practice. “Obviously, he has been on the commissioner’s exempt list, dealing with a matter involving a significant other,” Rapoport said. Of course, his legal matter was settled several weeks ago, and at that point, it was really just when would the NFL investigation take place?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Would they be able to see a video of the incident? They have not,” Rapoport continued. “I would say Jacobs has been preliminarily cleared and is expected to play this week. He is going to practice. He’s going to be on the field. They say he has kept in good shape, and the Green Bay Packers, who have had a really solid start to the season, probably could use a little bit of an improved running game, and they get Josh Jacobs in Week 7 to come in and do it.” From @GMFB : #Packers RB Josh Jacobs is back on the field today after a stint on the exempt list. pic.twitter.com/HnbaS1sMLO — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 21, 2026 The Packers could use Jacobs as the team averages 59.8 rushing yards per game, which is the lowest in the league. Subsequently, in Jacobs’ first season with Green Bay, he rushed for 1,329 yards with 15 touchdowns and in 2025, the former first-round pick recorded 929 yards with 13 touchdowns in 15 games. At any rate, it remains to be seen how the situation with Jacobs develops regarding a future suspension from the NFL. Related: Packers OC is sick and tired of Aaron Banks’ injury ‘roller coaster’ Related: Brewers’ World Series momentum capturing city’s attention over Packers

item.title: Jets, Aaron Glenn make Breece Hall decision
item.description: The New York Jets have clarified their plans for the backfield as running back Breece Hall works toward a return from injury during the 2026 NFL season. Head coach Aaron Glenn confirmed Wednesday that Hall will remain the team’s starting running back when he returns to the lineup, although Braelon Allen will continue to receive opportunities. Aaron Glenn on RB roles when Breece Hall returns based on how Braelon Allen has been playing: “Breece is our starter, he’s always been our starter, but Braelon is going to get touches too.” — Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) October 21, 2026 “Breece is our starter, he’s always been our starter, but Braelon is going to get touches too,” Glenn said. The announcement provides clarity on the Jets’ running back situation as they prepare for their Week 7 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. However, Hall’s availability for Sunday remains uncertain as he continues recovering from a quadriceps injury. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 7 of 2026 NFL season Hall remains Jets’ starting running back Sep 27, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; New York Jets running back Breece Hall (20) leaves the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Hall, 25, has not played since Week 3 because of the injury. He will not return to practice Wednesday, but he could get back onto the field later in the week. The Jets have not ruled him out for their divisional matchup against Miami. When Hall is healthy enough to return, he is expected to reclaim the leading role in New York’s backfield. Glenn’s comments indicate that the team still views Hall as its primary running back despite his extended absence. Hall’s return would provide a boost to a Jets offense looking to establish greater consistency on the ground. His ability to handle a significant workload has made him an important part of the team’s offensive plans, and New York will be eager to have him available again. Still, the coaching staff appears committed to maintaining a role for Allen, regardless of when Hall returns. MORE: Cowboys, Giants rookies lead way in recent NFL defensive grades Braelon Allen earns continued opportunities Oct 18, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New York Jets running back Braelon Allen (0) runs with the ball in the first half against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. item.title: Prediction: Sri Lanka vs. England 3rd ODI lineups and pitch report for Rawalpindi — Who do you think will win?
item.description: Prediction: Sri Lanka vs. England 3rd ODI lineups and pitch report for Rawalpindi — Who do you think will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sri Lanka and England meet in Rawalpindi on Thursday with no points between them. Both lost to Pakistan, who now have one foot in next Saturday's final, so one of these sides must take a first positive step. Sri Lanka collapsed from 210 for 4 chasing 306 and lost by 37 runs. England were 120 for 1 needing 183 and still fell short by 87. It is barely a month since they last met, when Harry Brook's England won the ODI series 2-1. Both teams opted to bowl first against Pakistan because of the dew, and the surface showed some variable bounce late in the evening. The match starts at 1 p.m. local time, which is 1:30 PM IST. Sri Lanka vs. England prediction, who will win? England were 120 for 1 chasing 306 on Tuesday and only lost because Arafat Minhas produced a spell of 6 for 40, so the batting is in good order. Brook admitted they played the left-arm spinner too carefully, and a bolder approach against Sri Lanka's spinners should fix that. England beat these opponents by 89 and 223 runs in September. Sri Lanka's selection is hard to predict, and they lost their last five completed matches in a pattern of collapses, including the slide from 210 for 4 on Tuesday. Rawalpindi has been a true batting surface, and any total near 300 makes the chase tough. The Cricket News Prediction: England to win. Sri Lanka vs. England predicted lineups, team news for 3rd ODI Here's how we think both sides will line up in this game. item.title: Pistons’ Ausar Thompson displays an assertive mindset to open Year 4
item.description: DETROIT — Kevin Huerter's missed 3-point shot set up Ausar Thompson to complete a move he hasn't made since high school. Huerter's miss led to two Boston Celtics players missing the defensive rebound, allowing Daniss Jenkins to secure the offensive board. Once the Detroit Pistons secured possession, Jenkins passed to Thompson, who had an open lane to the basket. Celtics guard Hugo Gonzalez jumped to Thompson's right side to defend the shot, but the 6-foot-7 versatile forward spun left, completed a 360-degree layup, and finished with his right hand. "When I saw him jump to my right side, I was like, 'I've been waiting on this moment.' I knew I had that in my bag," Thompson said. "I knew I was going to make it." 360 SPINNING LAYUP.Sweet move by Ausar Thompson on NBC and Peacock 😳 https://t.co/e46aKoXRZu — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 As the sell-out crowd inside Little Caesars Arena roared in astonishment, the move validated Thompson. It marked the first time Thompson attempted the move since his rookie season, in a game against the Minnesota Timberwolves. At the time, he missed the attempt after Rudy Gobert fouled him to prevent the highlight play. Years later, Thompson's layup became a notable moment in the Pistons' 121-113 season-opening win over the Celtics on Tuesday afternoon . Thompson recorded a double-double, finishing with 11 points and 11 rebounds. However, his 360 layup showed his determination to take a more assertive approach on offense as he enters his fourth season. "Being attack-minded offensively, getting to the paint, offensive rebounding, defensive rebounding, pushing the ball," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. "We know he’s going to guard the other guy’s best player and do what he does there, but how disruptive can he be on that end of the floor? We just want him to be assertive for as many minutes as he’s on the floor. We want everybody to feel his impact, so we just got to keep pushing him, and I know he wants it, so that’s the easy part for us." More: How Cade Cunningham will benefit from Pistons improved floor spacing Thompson has always approached the game aggressively, but his assertiveness has generally focused more on defense. However, his mindset hasn't always aligned with his offensive approach. While he has made solid contributions on offense, Thompson's limitations have at times made him somewhat passive during his first three years in the league. He missed opportunities to take the helm as a scorer, given how often he passed up shots in the past. Even with the ball, Thompson sometimes seemed hesitant to take on a facilitating role, despite entering the league as a capable playmaker and ball handler. Since training camp began, Thompson has said he wants to play outside his comfort zone. He said this approach stemmed from his confidence in the work he put in this summer, as he showed his newfound offensive aggression against the Celtics. "I see my role as being aggressive, doing what my coaches and teammates need from me,
item.content:encoded: DETROIT — Kevin Huerter's missed 3-point shot set up Ausar Thompson to complete a move he hasn't made since high school. Huerter's miss led to two Boston Celtics players missing the defensive rebound, allowing Daniss Jenkins to secure the offensive board. Once the Detroit Pistons secured possession, Jenkins passed to Thompson, who had an open lane to the basket. Celtics guard Hugo Gonzalez jumped to Thompson's right side to defend the shot, but the 6-foot-7 versatile forward spun left, completed a 360-degree layup, and finished with his right hand. "When I saw him jump to my right side, I was like, 'I've been waiting on this moment.' I knew I had that in my bag," Thompson said. "I knew I was going to make it." 360 SPINNING LAYUP.Sweet move by Ausar Thompson on NBC and Peacock 😳 https://t.co/e46aKoXRZu — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 As the sell-out crowd inside Little Caesars Arena roared in astonishment, the move validated Thompson. It marked the first time Thompson attempted the move since his rookie season, in a game against the Minnesota Timberwolves. At the time, he missed the attempt after Rudy Gobert fouled him to prevent the highlight play. Years later, Thompson's layup became a notable moment in the Pistons' 121-113 season-opening win over the Celtics on Tuesday afternoon . Thompson recorded a double-double, finishing with 11 points and 11 rebounds. However, his 360 layup showed his determination to take a more assertive approach on offense as he enters his fourth season. "Being attack-minded offensively, getting to the paint, offensive rebounding, defensive rebounding, pushing the ball," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. "We know he’s going to guard the other guy’s best player and do what he does there, but how disruptive can he be on that end of the floor? We just want him to be assertive for as many minutes as he’s on the floor. We want everybody to feel his impact, so we just got to keep pushing him, and I know he wants it, so that’s the easy part for us." More: How Cade Cunningham will benefit from Pistons improved floor spacing Thompson has always approached the game aggressively, but his assertiveness has generally focused more on defense. However, his mindset hasn't always aligned with his offensive approach. While he has made solid contributions on offense, Thompson's limitations have at times made him somewhat passive during his first three years in the league. He missed opportunities to take the helm as a scorer, given how often he passed up shots in the past. Even with the ball, Thompson sometimes seemed hesitant to take on a facilitating role, despite entering the league as a capable playmaker and ball handler. Since training camp began, Thompson has said he wants to play outside his comfort zone. He said this approach stemmed from his confidence in the work he put in this summer, as he showed his newfound offensive aggression against the Celtics. "I see my role as being aggressive, doing what my coaches and teammates need from me," Thompson said. "They have been telling me that they need me to be more aggressive, and that is what I am going to do." Thompson's mindset showed in the confident way he played in the final seconds of the fourth quarter, when he connected on a crossover, mid-range pull-up jumper over Celtics center Neemias Queta. That shot sealed the game for the Pistons. Although Thompson felt pressured to take the shot as the shot clock wound down, his willingness to attempt it speaks to his approach. In prior years, Thompson might have passed instead. Another indication of his approach this year came from the Pistons' desire to use him as a secondary ball-handler and playmaker. Against the Celtics, he looked more comfortable and confident running the offense, which led to him recording five assists. With Thompson as a playmaker, the Pistons seem to be pushing the pace faster than in the last three years. One of his standout moments as a playmaker occurred at the 7:19 mark of the first quarter, when Thompson delivered a no-look pass to John Collins on a fast break, leaving the Celtics' defenders momentarily puzzled. "That is going to make us harder to guard. The way they are gonna have to play him is going to be different," Bickerstaff said. "It allows us to be able to hide Deuce (Cade Cunningham) a little bit and get him in some action to bring him back to the ball. But we want Ausar to be aggressive. We want him to be assertive. All-around great game for Ausar. He makes us a better basketball team." More: Meet the 2026-27 Pistons: A player-by-player breakdown While much of Thompson's improved aggression stems from his offense, it hasn't kept him from proving how he earned a spot on the league's All-Defensive First Team last season. Thompson was the primary defender against Celtics star Jayson Tatum. He limited the six-time All-Star to one of his worst shooting nights, shooting 6-of-23 from the field and 0-of-7 from behind the arc. Since being selected with the fifth overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, Thompson has established himself as arguably the league's top perimeter defender. Last season, Thompson led the league in steals, averaging 2.0 per game and totaling 146. His defensive impact went beyond takeaways; his versatility also earned him 69 blocks and 5.7 rebounds over 73 games. As a result, his defensive production led the Pistons to reward Thompson with a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension in September. If Thompson can maintain his assertiveness on offense while continuing his defensive dominance, he could not only increase his recognition as a two-way star but also keep the Pistons' championship aspirations realistic in a formidable Eastern Conference. coty.davis@detroitnews.com @cotydavis_24 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Pistons’ Ausar Thompson displays an assertive mindset to open Year 4

item.title: Pirates Year in Review 2026: Looking Back at Braxton Ashcraft's Season
item.description: Pirates Year in Review 2026: Looking Back at Braxton Ashcraft's Season originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It took a long path through the minor leagues, including Tommy John surgery, but in 2026, the Pirates finally reaped the benefits of drafting Braxton Ashcraft in the second round of the 2018 MLB Draft. Ashcraft spent five years in the minor leagues before making his MLB debut in 2025, primarily coming out of the bullpen. But in 2026, he didn't just become a full-time starter — he was one of the better pitchers in the National League. Here's a look back at Ashcraft's breakout 2026 season for the Pirates, becoming an All-Star. MORE: Looking back at Oneil Cruz's 2026 season for Pirates Pirates Year in Review 2026: Braxton Ashcraft Ashcraft faced a ton of adversity to reach his 2026 breakout season. Coming out of high school in Texas, he was a second-round pick to the Pirates in 2018. But after logging a 5.77 ERA in Low-A, he also underwent surgery on his left shoulder and a torn meniscus, missed time to the canceled 2020 season, came back in 2021 before needing Tommy John surgery, then spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons ramping back up to a high level. It was a worthwhile wait in the end, though. Last season, Ashcraft looked strong over 26 appearances and eight starts for Pittsburgh, and he took it to the next level in 2026. From his first All-Star nod to a complete game and 173 strikeouts, Ashcraft fully emerged as a top arm behind Paul Skenes in the Pirates' rotation, which became a strength. Now 27 years old, the Pirates are certainly happy with where Ashcraft is at, blossoming into one of the best starters in the NL after years of injury issues. While his season came to an early end in September as the Pirates grew more cautious with his workload, he was arguably the most reliable pitcher on the roster. Braxton Ashcraft's most memorable moment For a pitcher who had undergone multiple surgeries in the minor leagues and totaled under 70 MLB innings in 2025, it was even more of an accomplishment to pitch a complete game for the Pirates in August. Already on pace to take on a career-high workload, Ashcraft dominated against the Marlins on Aug. 13, needing just 85 pitches to beat Miami while striking out 10 batters. Braxton Ashcraft stats for 2026 season Starts IP ERA WHIP K BB K/9 bWAR fWAR 28 165.1 3.65 1.09 173 35 9.4 3.5 3.5 Ashcraft ranked among the NL leaders in wins (5th), strikeouts (13th) and WHIP (6th), a true breakout campaign as he was named to his first All-Star Game in July. Looking ahead to 2027, the hope is that he can trend closer to the 200-inning threshold as he gets further removed from his major surgeries in the minor leagues. Ashcraft looks like he can be one of the top strikeout pitchers in baseball if he stays on the mound for a full season. The Pirates came into 2026 knowing they had one ace in Skenes. They may have another on their hands if Ashcraf

Already on pace to take on a career-high workload, Ashcraft dominated against the Marlins on Aug. 13, needing just 85 pitches to beat Miami while striking out 10 batters. Braxton Ashcraft stats for 2026 season Starts IP ERA WHIP K BB K/9 bWAR fWAR 28 165.1 3.65 1.09 173 35 9.4 3.5 3.5 Ashcraft ranked among the NL leaders in wins (5th), strikeouts (13th) and WHIP (6th), a true breakout campaign as he was named to his first All-Star Game in July. Looking ahead to 2027, the hope is that he can trend closer to the 200-inning threshold as he gets further removed from his major surgeries in the minor leagues. Ashcraft looks like he can be one of the top strikeout pitchers in baseball if he stays on the mound for a full season. The Pirates came into 2026 knowing they had one ace in Skenes. They may have another on their hands if Ashcraft can improve in any fashion again next season. item.title: Jaguars drop in NFL power rankings entering Week 7
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs with the ball during the NFL London Series match between Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars enter their Week 7 bye with a sour taste in their mouth after losing to the division rival Houston Texans. Still, the Jags are in the driver’s seat in the AFC South. They’re feeling good about where they’re at through a third of the season. “We strung together some good performances,” safety Eric Murray said Tuesday. “I think the biggest thing going forward is just hitting on consistency and getting back to what we do on a more consistent basis. Not necessarily putting ourselves in bad positions where we can’t make plays and going off of that but just being more consistent. We are 4-2 at the bye, it’s nothing to be going crazy about. It’s just lock in and keep going.” As Week 7 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense of how the Jaguars are viewed nationally. Pro Football Talk: 4 (last week: 3) From Mike Florio : They’re finally getting a return on the Travis Hunter investment. ESPN: 5 (5) From Michael DiRocco : Penalties have cost the Jaguars three touchdowns, including a pair of 3-yard touchdown runs by running back Bhayshul Tuten. It happened again in Sunday’s loss, with a questionable holding call on tight end Brenton Strange. The Jaguars didn’t get points on that possession because QB Trevor Lawrence threw an end zone interception two plays later. Jacksonville did score touchdowns after the other two penalties, against New England and Cincinnati, but it finally caught up to them in a three-point loss to the Texans. NFL.com: 5 (5) From Nick Shook : The Jaguars’ high-scoring loss to the Texans at Wembley Stadium was one of the best games of the season so far. Two division rivals battled for four quarters, and the Jaguars erased a 10-point deficit, but they had to still be irritated as they flew home from their two-week trip after a last-second defeat. Travis Hunter’s emergence should be monitored going forward — his two-way ability is finally adding significant value to the Jaguars’ larger equation. Jaguars fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Jaguars polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Big Cat Country fans. Then discuss the results with Duval. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Bleacher Report: 7 (5) From Kris Knox : Jacksonville features an elite run defense and boasts an offense that can match points with anyone when Trevor Lawrence is taking care of the football. That could be enough for the Jags to control the AFC South and push into the postseason with plenty of momentum. However, it’s fair to wonder if Jacksonville can corral top signal-callers in January. The Athletic: 7 (5) From Josh Kendall and Chad Graff : Fantasy focus: Trevor Lawrenc

Still, the Jags are in the driver’s seat in the AFC South. It’s just lock in and keep going.” As Week 7 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense of how the Jaguars are viewed nationally. Pro Football Talk: 4 (last week: 3) From Mike Florio : They’re finally getting a return on the Travis Hunter investment. ESPN: 5 (5) From Michael DiRocco : Penalties have cost the Jaguars three touchdowns, including a pair of 3-yard touchdown runs by running back Bhayshul Tuten. It happened again in Sunday’s loss, with a questionable holding call on tight end Brenton Strange. The Jaguars didn’t get points on that possession because QB Trevor Lawrence threw an end zone interception two plays later. Jacksonville did score touchdowns after the other two penalties, against New England and Cincinnati, but it finally caught up to them in a three-point loss to the Texans. NFL.com: 5 (5) From Nick Shook : The Jaguars’ high-scoring loss to the Texans at Wembley Stadium was one of the best games of the season so far. Two division rivals battled for four quarters, and the Jaguars erased a 10-point deficit, but they had to still be irritated as they flew home from their two-week trip after a last-second defeat. Travis Hunter’s emergence should be monitored going forward — his two-way ability is finally adding significant value to the Jaguars’ larger equation. Jaguars fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Jaguars polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Big Cat Country fans. Then discuss the results with Duval. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Bleacher Report: 7 (5) From Kris Knox : Jacksonville features an elite run defense and boasts an offense that can match points with anyone when Trevor Lawrence is taking care of the football. That could be enough for the Jags to control the AFC South and push into the postseason with plenty of momentum. However, it’s fair to wonder if Jacksonville can corral top signal-callers in January. The Athletic: 7 (5) From Josh Kendall and Chad Graff : Fantasy focus: Trevor Lawrence. The Jags quarterback is outperforming his draft position by more than 50 spots. He went off the board an average of 86th, but he’s 22nd in scoring (19.0 ppg) through six games. Lawrence’s EPA per dropback this season (0.20) is nearly twice his career high, and Jacksonville lost Sunday despite a four-touchdown, one-interception performance from its leader on offense. USA Today: 7 (5) From Nate Davis : CB/WR Travis Hunter played a season-high 71 snaps Sunday, quite a few of them impactful, and the Jags lost − through no fault of Hunter, who’s played nearly every defensive snap the past three weeks. Still trying to find his sweet spot, but we may finally be near it. Same can’t be said for WR Brian Thomas Jr. Sports Illustrated: 8 (2) From Conor Orr : It’s hard to penalize the Jaguars that much for a shootout loss to the heating-up Texans. But if Travis Hunter can do this and this in the same game, and we can inch him on the field more after possibly trading Brian Thomas Jr., I like the ceiling for this team. CBS Sports: 8 (5) From Pete Prisco : They have to do a better job rushing the passer if they are to be a deep-playoff team. They have to make a move to get somebody at the trade deadline. Fox Sports: 8 (5) From Ralph Vacchiano : The Jaguars’ offense is finally starting to click, but their 34-31 loss to the Texans in London should be a wake-up call that their defense isn’t everything they thought it was. Maybe they were just tired from a long couple of weeks in London, or maybe the Texans are just starting to roll. But even Houston’s disastrous running game managed to put up 114 yards on the Jags. The good news for them, though, is they have a really soft schedule coming out of the bye week, including games against the Colts and the Giants and two meetings with the Titans. So the Jags have a good chance to get back on their roll. Yahoo Sports: 9 (5) From Frank Schwab : The Jaguars looked very good through four weeks, but the London trip was not great for them. They were very lucky to escape with a 1-1 record on the trip, thanks to Philadelphia’s game-management error gifting Jacksonville a last-second field goal to win. Their defense had a big letdown against Houston as it allowed C.J. Stroud to pick apart the Jaguars. Instead of knocking the Texans out of the AFC South race, Houston now lingers with an easy four-game stretch of its schedule coming up. It was a very disappointing outcome for a team that looked like it was one of the few to look like a trustworthy contender after the season’s first month. Still, a 4-2 start isn’t a bad outcome, and the Jaguars don’t seem concerned. WEEK 6 OBJECTIVE NFL POWER RANKINGS — The Rams fell!! But narrowly on top. Sorry,,, — Ok yes the Chargers are bad — Goodbye Eagles — Here come the Texans! pic.twitter.com/zfFwwU8MfS — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) October 21, 2026 Where would you rank the team, Jaguars fans? item.title: Mid-Major Madness Reacts Survey: Which mid-major will be ranked first?
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - MARCH 14: Head coach Josh Schertz talks to his team in a timeout against the Loyola Ramblers during the quarterfinal round of the A10 basketball tournament at Capital One Arena on March 14, 2025 in Washington, DC. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NCAA. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Mid-Major fans and fans across the country. The AP preseason men’s basketball poll was released earlier this week, and while no mid-majors cracked the initial top 25, six of them received votes. So, for this week’s reacts questions, we’re asking which of the six mid-majors that received votes in the AP preseason poll is most likely to first appear in the rankings? Saint Louis, VCU, Nevada, Grand Canyon, Utah State, or Santa Clara are the contenders here. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Saint Louis The Billikens spent a large chunk of last season ranked, and there’s reason to believe Josh Schertz’s team will be in the mix to be a top-25 team once again. There’s still uncertainty around whether Robbie Avila will be granted a fifth year, but SLU has several impact players this season. Trey Green poured in 10.7 points per game last season and shot 44% from beyond the arc. Kellen Thames contributed 9.7 points and 4.7 rebounds on 65% shooting a season ago. Both were preseason all-A-10 first team selections. Amari McCottry added 10.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.9 assist. Saint Louis has notable non-conference games against Missouri, High Point, Saint Mary’s, Grand Canyon, South Florida and DePaul. VCU The Rams won the Atlantic-10 tournament championship last season and were picked as the preseason favorites this year. Phil Martelli Jr.’s squad is loaded once again. Lazar Djokovic tallied 13.2 points and 5.2 rebounds a game while shooting 50% from the floor last season. Reigning A10 Rookie of the Year Nyk Lewis poured in 8.7 points and 4.5 rebounds. Brandon Jennings contributed 8.5 points, 3.6 boards and 1.7 steals per game. VCU visits Memphis and Santa Clara in its first four games before heading to Maui with a date with Providence in the opener and potentially Arizona in round two. Florida Atlantic and Mississippi State are also part of the non-conference. Nevada Steve Alford has the Wolf Pack looking at a run for the Mountain West title in his swan-song season. Nevada went to the NIT quarterfinals last season and brings back several players. Elijah Price notched 12.8 points and 8.5 rebounds. Vaughn Weems served as a double-digit scorer last year with 10.1 points and 4.2 rebounds. Peyton White is also back after contributing 4.6 points and 1.7 rebounds as a freshman. Notable non-conference games for the Wolf Pack include against Saint Mary’s at Lake Tahoe and San Francisco and Santa Clara in the Acrisure Series. Grand Canyon The Lopes look to take advantage of the mass exodus from the Mountain West as they enter their second year in

Vaughn Weems served as a double-digit scorer last year with 10.1 points and 4.2 rebounds. Peyton White is also back after contributing 4.6 points and 1.7 rebounds as a freshman. Notable non-conference games for the Wolf Pack include against Saint Mary’s at Lake Tahoe and San Francisco and Santa Clara in the Acrisure Series. Grand Canyon The Lopes look to take advantage of the mass exodus from the Mountain West as they enter their second year in the conference. GCU ranks 44th in KenPom and 42nd in BartTorvik. Dylan Darling comes to Phoenix after a season at St. John’s where he averaged 6.9 points, 2.6 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals. Jaden Henley was a standout last year with 17.7 points, 2.9 assists and 1.6 steals per game. Makaih Williams was also in double figures with 14 points and 2.5 assists. Efe Demirel had a solid freshman season for the Lopes with 8.5 points 5.3 boards and 1.1 blocks. Caleb Shaw added 7.8 points and 3.8 rebounds. Utah State No matter who the coach is, Utah State is one of the top mid-majors every year. Four straight NCAA Tournament appearances with three different head coaches. In comes Ben Jacobson, and expect the results to be the same. Mason Falslev returns to Logan after averaging 16 points, 5.7 rebounds and three assists last season. Karson Templin is back with the Aggies too after 8.8 points and 4.2 boards. Will Hornseth came to USU with Jacobson from Northern Iowa after posting 11.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists. Dallin Hall ranked 19th in assist-to-turnover ratio (3.27) at Virginia and came back to his home state. AJ Bates joined the program after posting 12.1 points, 5.9 assists, 2.8 boards and 1.2 steals at Louisiana Tech. The Aggies have matchups with UC San Diego, SMU, USC, New Mexico, BYU and Tulsa in the non-conference before their inaugural season in the Pac-12. Santa Clara The Broncos reached the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 1996 last season, and Herb Sendek’s squad enters this year as the preseason favorite in the WCC. Jake Ensminger notched 6.5 points, 5.5 rebounds and 2.9 assists for a 3.2 assist-to-tunrover ratio. Sash Gavalyugov came on strong at the WCC Tournament with a statline of nine points, 14 boards and 5.7 assists. Thierry Darlan is also back after averaging 6.1 points and 3.6 rebounds. Santa Clara faces New Mexico, VCU, Nevada, GCU, Murray State, McNeese, Boise State and Oregon State in the non-conference.

item.title: Journo spots Carrick having a ‘robust exchange of views’ with Man Utd starter in first half vs Como
item.description: Journo spots Carrick having a ‘robust exchange of views’ with Man Utd starter in first half vs Como Manchester United have got off to a nightmare start once again in the Champions League by conceding early. Last time out in Europe, Atletico Madrid opened the scoring inside the first minute of action before going on to seal a 2-0 win. Tonight, Como broke the deadlock in just the second minute via a scintillating strike from Nico Paz, making United the first English team in history to concede in the first two minutes of consecutive major European matches, as per Opta. It’s therefore no surprise that, shortly after the opener and United’s torrid start, Samuel Luckhurst spotted Michael Carrick bickering with Matheus Cunha from the touchline. “Carrick just had a relatively robust exchange of views with Cunha during the stoppage before he cursed at MUFC losing possession again,” Luckhurst penned on Twitter/X. Cesc Fabregas’ side have dominated in the first half, and arguably played United off the park for the first half-hour of action. United are now at risk of suffering the same fate they did at the Metropolitano, where they had only very few chances and failed to get back into the game with even one goal. Prior to kick-off, Dimitar Berbatov expressed just how essential it was that his former club left with a win tonight. “If they lose today, the pressure will be even more. They need the win today no matter what. I don’t care how. Long ball, direct ball, possession — just get the win because the pressure will get less after the game,” the ex-striker said on TNT Sports. United’s last win in any competition came on September 10 against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah, while their last Premier League victory was all the way back in August against newly-promoted Ipswich Town. item.title: Rio Ngumoha overtakes Balotelli in Champions League record
item.description: Rio Ngumoha overtakes Balotelli in Champions League record Liverpool forward Rio Ngumoha became the third-youngest player to register two assists in a Champions League match during the Reds' 4-3 win over Villarreal . The 18-year-old provided both assists to move ahead of former Liverpool striker Mario Balotelli , who was 18 years and two months old when he achieved the feat for Inter against Anorthosis in 2008. Only Warren Zaïre-Emery and Theo Walcott were younger when they registered two assists in a Champions League match. Zaïre-Emery was 17 years, seven months and 18 days old when he set up two goals for Paris St-Germain against AC Milan in 2023, while Walcott was 17 years and eight months old when he did so for Arsenal against Hamburg in 2006. Ngumoha had already made history in August 2025, becoming Liverpool's youngest goalscorer at the age of 17 years and one month. If he scores in this season's Champions League, he will also become the club's youngest goalscorer in the competition. That record belongs to Trent Alexander-Arnold , who was 19 years and 11 days old when he scored. Ngumoha has made nine appearances this season and recently made his senior England debut. item.title: No Ebola in Niger, state on high alert — Health Director
item.description: By Clare Nnabuike, Minna The Niger State Government has assured residents that no Ebola case has been detected in the state, saying it has activated emergency response measures to prevent a possible outbreak. The Director of Public Health in the state Ministry of Health, Dr Ibrahim Idris, gave the assurance on Wednesday during a telephone conversation with our correspondent. Idris said the state was on high alert because of its proximity to the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), where a Ugandan woman was reportedly arrested over suspected exposure to Ebola. He urged residents to remain calm, continue their normal activities and observe necessary health precautions. The director said no person identified as a contact of the suspected case had entered Niger State, adding that the government was taking preventive measures to keep the disease out. Although Niger shares a boundary with the FCT, Idris said the state had not recorded any Ebola case and was strengthening its preparedness because of the severity of the disease. “Niger State has no Ebola outbreak, and the citizens should stay calm. We have already activated the emergency operation, and we will ensure that there is no outbreak of Ebola in the state,” he said. Idris said the state was monitoring the situation and taking steps to prevent people identified as contacts of the woman from introducing the disease into the state. “The state is doing everything to ensure that the 44 contacts said to have met the Ugandan woman do not enter Niger State. We have already activated our emergency operation. We will not give the disease any chances,” he said. He disclosed that the state held a high-level health meeting on Wednesday to assess its response measures, with particular attention to the reported Ebola concern in the FCT. The director urged residents to observe basic hygiene measures, including regular handwashing, and follow relevant public health advice. He also disclosed that the state was nearing completion of an isolation centre as part of measures to strengthen its preparedness for any suspected case. “As I am talking to you, we have almost completed our isolation centre, and we are putting other measures in place. We don’t want to leave anything to chance,” Idris said. The post No Ebola in Niger, state on high alert — Health Director appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Texas ranked 7th, Houston 10th in first AP NCAA men's basketball poll
item.description: Texas' strong close to the 2025-26 season and a stellar offseason have the Longhorns seventh in the initial Associated Press men's basketball rankings. Two other Texas teams that won NCAA tournament games last year are also ranked, with Houston at 10 and Texas Tech at 19. Florida is No. 1 Florida led the first poll for a 2026-27 season that officially starts on Nov. 1, garnering 47 of 59 first-place votes. Duke got 10 first-place votes and is ranked No. 2, while No. 3 Illinois got two first-place votes. Defending national champion Michigan is No. 16. More: New faces, new league, big questions for UTEP Miners men's basketball The only Mountain West team to receive votes was Nevada, which got two votes, tying it for 41st. The top Big 12 team is Arizona, checking in at fifth. The SEC has seven ranked teams, the Big 12 has six, while the Big 10 and ACC each have four. Texas is projected to start three transfers and a freshman as it builds on the momentum of last year's run to the Sweet 16. Texas' offseason was rated the best in the country by ESPN . When does the NCAA college basketball season start? The first official game of the 2026-27 season is on Nov. 1, when Notre Dame plays Villanova at the Palazzetto dello Sport in Rome, Italy, at 7:30 a.m. MT/8:30 p.m. CT. More: Florida leads men's basketball preseason coaches poll. See where Duke, UConn, others rank Bret Bloomquist can be reached at bbloomquist@elpasotimes.com; @Bretbloomquist on X. item.title: No Goals in Nine: Why Rangers Must Replace Djeidi Gassama – Opinion
item.description: Rangers v Middlesbrough - Pre-Season Friendly Rangers FC graphics are outside the stadium during the pre-season friendly match between Glasgow Rangers and Middlesbrough at Ibrox Park in Glasgow, Scotland, on July 26, 2025. Glasgow Strathclyde U… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ricky Carroll, Editor It might have been Albert Einstein who said something about the definition of madness or insanity being to perform the same action over and over again, but expecting different results, just as Rangers are with Djeidi Gassama. The 23-year-old winger arrived from Sheffield Wednesday in a cut-price £2 million deal last summer, with Owls fans feeling that Danny Rohl had taken advantage of a loophole that saw them robbed of a £10 million transfer windfall. Rangers looked to have pulled a blinder when Gassama hit the ground running in the Europa League qualifiers, only to become the latest in a long line of frustrating wide men. Time for Rangers to Drop Djeidi Gassama IMAGO / Focus Images The Mauritania international has been around professional football for some time and is approaching 200 senior appearances. By now, he should have ironed out the creases that he left Paris Saint-Germain’s academy with as a player with high expectations. His consistency and availability are to be applauded; his end product isn’t. Gassama featured in every league game for Rangers last term and has done so again this term – 47 in total. What frustrates, much like Ryan Kent, isn’t his work rate, attitude, durability, ball carrying, or ability to create space for teammates; it is his goal return. He has one goal in 14 games this season in total, none in the league, to add to his three from last year. Read More: Rangers’ Next £20m Star? Transfer Interest Reported From Top Leagues in Key Man The 10 assists in 70 appearances since he joined is hardly the sort of figure that inspires confidence either. With the same minutes, Scott Wright, Ross McCausland and Rabbi Matondo could all have produced something similar. With Kim Minsu and Badredine Bouanani both proficient dribblers and attacking options, Rangers no longer need to rely on Gassama being the only outlet to progress the play up the park, and it is time for Derek McInnes to give someone else a chance. What Has McInnes Said About Gassama? There is a feeling that every game is going to be the one. But it doesn’t come. Against Dundee, Bouanani did his job on the other flank and was Rangers’ most dangerous player, and yet it was Gassama who played the full 90 minutes. Every shot that Bouanani hit was placed and put on target; only two world-class saves denied him a hat-trick. Despite his fleeting appearances, he looks like the complete package. Gassama though, as McInnes himself admitted recently, via The Rangers Review , needs to start adding numbers: “Particularly in recent weeks he has carried the fight. We’ve built the game well, utilised space and become a very good counter-attacking team, and he’s been a big part of that.

Glasgow Strathclyde U… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ricky Carroll, Editor It might have been Albert Einstein who said something about the definition of madness or insanity being to perform the same action over and over again, but expecting different results, just as Rangers are with Djeidi Gassama. Time for Rangers to Drop Djeidi Gassama IMAGO / Focus Images The Mauritania international has been around professional football for some time and is approaching 200 senior appearances. He has one goal in 14 games this season in total, none in the league, to add to his three from last year. Read More: Rangers’ Next £20m Star? Transfer Interest Reported From Top Leagues in Key Man The 10 assists in 70 appearances since he joined is hardly the sort of figure that inspires confidence either. With the same minutes, Scott Wright, Ross McCausland and Rabbi Matondo could all have produced something similar. With Kim Minsu and Badredine Bouanani both proficient dribblers and attacking options, Rangers no longer need to rely on Gassama being the only outlet to progress the play up the park, and it is time for Derek McInnes to give someone else a chance. What Has McInnes Said About Gassama? There is a feeling that every game is going to be the one. But it doesn’t come. Against Dundee, Bouanani did his job on the other flank and was Rangers’ most dangerous player, and yet it was Gassama who played the full 90 minutes. Every shot that Bouanani hit was placed and put on target; only two world-class saves denied him a hat-trick. Despite his fleeting appearances, he looks like the complete package. Gassama though, as McInnes himself admitted recently, via The Rangers Review , needs to start adding numbers: “Particularly in recent weeks he has carried the fight. We’ve built the game well, utilised space and become a very good counter-attacking team, and he’s been a big part of that. “Gas just needs to improve his numbers. He’s desperate to score more goals, and it’s something he’s aware of. Whether it’s attacking crosses from the opposite side or creating opportunities himself, that’s the one thing he needs to add to his game. “Because the fitness is there, the intent is there, the power is there, and the confidence is there. It’s just that final piece and, if we can put everything together, hopefully he can continue progressing and become a big player for us this season.” Daisuke Yokota being injured has reduced McInnes’ options, although Findlay Curtis and Minsu could both play off the left-hand side of the attack if he wanted to make the change. The Last Word There is no denying that Gassama has everything needed to be a key player for Rangers if they are to win the Scottish Premiership and other domestic trophies this season. He can create something from nothing, and he can score goals when little seems on, but as Light Blues fans saw with Kent, carrying a winger that works hard and plays every game means little when they aren’t scoring goals or creating good chances for their teammates when it comes to silverware at the end of the season. item.title: BioWare Officially Shutting Down and New Mass Effect Canceled
item.description: Electronic Arts is making big cuts, including laying off staff and shutting down storied developer BioWare, the studio behind the Mass Effect and Dragon Age franchises. The closure of BioWare means that the next Mass Effect game, colloquially known as Mass Effect 5 , which was announced in 2020 , has been canceled.

item.title: 2023 Obi-Datti Campaign leaders dump Obi, back Tinubu
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Some former members of the 2023 Presidential Campaign Council of the Labour Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, have defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027. The former campaign officials, under a new political platform known as Batified Obidients, also endorsed Vice-President Kashim Shettima for a second term and pledged to mobilise former Obidient supporters and voters in opposition strongholds for Tinubu’s re-election. The group announced its decision at a press conference in Abuja on Tuesday, citing what it described as leadership and organisational weaknesses in the Obi-Datti campaign, as well as its assessment of the Tinubu administration’s reform agenda. Led by Adesina Fagbenro-Byron, former Director of Operations of the Obi-Datti Presidential Campaign Council, the group said it had adopted the APC as its political platform for the 2027 general election. Reading the group’s statement, Fabian Ozoigbo Chukwudoruo, former Head of Logistics of the Obi-Datti campaign and Deputy National Coordinator of Batified Obidients, said the decision was informed by the need to promote good governance and sustainable national development. Fagbenro-Byron said, “Today, we have made our choice. Let there be no ambiguity. We are coming together again. “We are former Labour Party and Obidient supporters. We are now shifting our support to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and adopting the All Progressives Congress, the APC, as our political vehicle for 2027, under the name Batified Obidients.” Why we left Obi — Defectors Explaining their decision to leave Obi, the former campaign officials cited concerns over leadership, the management of competent personnel and the handling of internal disagreements within the campaign organisation. Fagbenro-Byron said members had voluntarily contributed their time, skills and, in some cases, personal resources to Obi’s campaign because they believed he represented a change in Nigeria’s political direction. However, he said their subsequent reflections had convinced them that the campaign failed to make adequate use of the expertise available to it. “After months of honest reflection on what we witnessed from inside the campaign, the truth became impossible to ignore. “We saw real weaknesses in how talent was mis-managed, how diversity was mis-handled, and how internal conflicts went unresolved. Competent people who offered their expertise were often left unappreciated or unrecognised,” he said. The group’s national coordinator said the shortcomings raised broader questions about Obi’s preparedness for the demands of governing Nigeria. “Looking back with clear eyes, we have come to see that the demands of leading a country as complex and demanding as Nigeria may have been beyond what Mr Peter Obi was prepared for,” he said. Fagbenro-Byron, however, acknowledged that the criticism did not necessarily mean Obi lacked sincere intentions.

item.content:encoded: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Some former members of the 2023 Presidential Campaign Council of the Labour Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, have defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027. The former campaign officials, under a new political platform known as Batified Obidients, also endorsed Vice-President Kashim Shettima for a second term and pledged to mobilise former Obidient supporters and voters in opposition strongholds for Tinubu’s re-election. The group announced its decision at a press conference in Abuja on Tuesday, citing what it described as leadership and organisational weaknesses in the Obi-Datti campaign, as well as its assessment of the Tinubu administration’s reform agenda. Led by Adesina Fagbenro-Byron, former Director of Operations of the Obi-Datti Presidential Campaign Council, the group said it had adopted the APC as its political platform for the 2027 general election. Reading the group’s statement, Fabian Ozoigbo Chukwudoruo, former Head of Logistics of the Obi-Datti campaign and Deputy National Coordinator of Batified Obidients, said the decision was informed by the need to promote good governance and sustainable national development. Fagbenro-Byron said, “Today, we have made our choice. Let there be no ambiguity. We are coming together again. “We are former Labour Party and Obidient supporters. We are now shifting our support to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and adopting the All Progressives Congress, the APC, as our political vehicle for 2027, under the name Batified Obidients.” Why we left Obi — Defectors Explaining their decision to leave Obi, the former campaign officials cited concerns over leadership, the management of competent personnel and the handling of internal disagreements within the campaign organisation. Fagbenro-Byron said members had voluntarily contributed their time, skills and, in some cases, personal resources to Obi’s campaign because they believed he represented a change in Nigeria’s political direction. However, he said their subsequent reflections had convinced them that the campaign failed to make adequate use of the expertise available to it. “After months of honest reflection on what we witnessed from inside the campaign, the truth became impossible to ignore. “We saw real weaknesses in how talent was mis-managed, how diversity was mis-handled, and how internal conflicts went unresolved. Competent people who offered their expertise were often left unappreciated or unrecognised,” he said. The group’s national coordinator said the shortcomings raised broader questions about Obi’s preparedness for the demands of governing Nigeria. “Looking back with clear eyes, we have come to see that the demands of leading a country as complex and demanding as Nigeria may have been beyond what Mr Peter Obi was prepared for,” he said. Fagbenro-Byron, however, acknowledged that the criticism did not necessarily mean Obi lacked sincere intentions. “This is not to say he did not try, or that his intentions were not sincere. But it became clear to those of us inside the campaign that he was, in many ways, out of his depth without fully realising it,” he added. He said the campaign had access to professionals willing to contribute their knowledge and experience, but their potential was not adequately utilised. The group clarified that its position reflected the experiences and conclusions of its members and did not represent all Nigerians who supported Obi in 2023. It also acknowledged that some former supporters had moved to other political parties, including the African Democratic Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, while others remained in the Labour Party. Tinubu’s reforms influenced our decision On why they chose to support Tinubu, the defectors cited their assessment of the administration’s policies and reforms over the past three years. While acknowledging the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, including hunger, rising living costs, insecurity and persistent gaps in healthcare and education, the group argued that the administration had initiated reforms capable of addressing longstanding structural problems. “The reforms have been difficult. They have been painful for many households. Hunger is real. The cost of living has bitten hard. Families are struggling to put food on the table,” Fagbenro-Byron said. He listed the removal of the petrol subsidy, increased allocations to state and local governments, student loan initiatives, local fertiliser production and reforms allowing greater state participation in the electricity market among the policies that influenced the group’s decision. The group also cited the Supreme Court’s affirmation of local government financial autonomy, saying it could strengthen grassroots development. “These are not finished victories. They are the foundations of a country that can produce more of what it needs instead of living forever on imports and artificial prices,” Fagbenro-Byron said. Batified Obidients also expressed support for the administration’s infrastructure programme, particularly projects associated with the Minister of Works, David Umahi; the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo; and the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake. The group said it wanted to see the projects completed and their anticipated benefits fully realised. Group plans grassroots mobilisation Beyond endorsing Tinubu and Shettima, the group said it would mobilise former campaign associates, undecided voters and other Nigerians to support the APC ahead of the 2027 general election. It said its activities would include membership registration, grassroots mobilisation, political organisation, rallies and campaigns, with particular attention to states where opposition candidates defeated Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election. Fagbenro-Byron said the group would seek to expand the president’s support base ahead of the next election. “We will mobilise our former colleagues, undecided voters, and other Nigerians who desire competent and inclusive governance. “We will work to grow the support President Tinubu received in 2023, with special attention to states where his opposition won,” he said. Explaining the group’s choice of name, he said its members remained committed to the demand for good governance that had driven the Obidient movement but now believed the APC offered the political platform through which to pursue that objective. “We do not deny our history. But we remain Obidient to the hunger for good governance. We are Batified in our recognition of competence, courage, and the direction needed to rebuild Nigeria. Our loyalty is to Nigeria first,” he said. He added that the group was not seeking to diminish other political parties but to build a broad coalition around the APC. “For us, the choice is clear: APC and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027,” he said. The post 2023 Obi-Datti Campaign leaders dump Obi, back Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: EA is shutting down BioWare
item.description: BioWare, the legendary studio behind RPGs like Mass Effect , Dragon Age , and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , is shutting down, the company confirmed in a statement . Alongside the closure, Electronic Arts has also chosen not to continue development on the next Mass Effect game that was in the works, according to an announcement sent to EA staff . The company is also laying off around 400 staffers, Bloomberg reports . The changes follow EA going private in a $55 billion deal that closed in August . "BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," Cam Weber, EA president … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Military pensions board chair vows to end payment delays
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The new Chairman of the Military Pensions Board (MPB), Major General Julius Ehioze Osifo, has pledged to tackle delays in the payment of pensions, gratuities and death benefits to retired military personnel and families of deceased service members. Osifo said delays in paying death benefits to the families of soldiers killed in action could undermine troop morale and dishonour the sacrifices of fallen military personnel. He made the pledge on Wednesday while formally taking over the leadership of the Board, promising to eliminate bureaucratic bottlenecks, deploy modern technology and streamline the processing of entitlements. Recalling his operational experience in Operation Hadin Kai in the North-East, Osifo said the military’s responsibility to its personnel extended beyond their years of active service to ensuring that their families were adequately supported after their death. He stressed that the sacrifices of personnel confronting security threats must be matched by an efficient pension administration system that guarantees prompt payment of entitlements to veterans and the families of fallen service members. Osifo said his administration would prioritise timely processing and payment of benefits while ensuring that legitimate beneficiaries received their entitlements without unnecessary delays. “My mission statement will be anchored on leading a Board that will prioritise all ways and means to ensure payments are prompt, accessed with seamless ease, less cumbersome, less bureaucratic, but with an overriding commitment to ensuring only the rightful recipients get their due entitlements,” he said. The new chairman assured military veterans and families of deceased personnel that his administration would improve access to benefits and reduce the difficulties associated with processing claims. He said the Board would adopt modern technology, strengthen collaboration with the military services to identify beneficiaries proactively and accelerate the processing of pensions, gratuities and death benefits. Osifo also pledged to deepen engagement with the Defence Headquarters, service headquarters, the Ministry of Defence, relevant National Assembly committees, the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation and the Ministry of Finance to improve coordination and facilitate payments. On staff welfare, he said the Board would invest in the capacity development and well-being of its military and civilian personnel, noting that a well-trained and motivated workforce was essential to efficient service delivery. He pledged to uphold high ethical and professional standards, strengthen training and ensure fair treatment of personnel. “The challenge to reposition the Board is a collective responsibility. In view of this, I implore all officers, servicemen and women, and civilian staff to brace up for the enormous task ahead. All hands must be on deck for the realisation of my vision,” he said.
