Osifo said delays in paying death benefits to the families of soldiers killed in action could undermine troop morale and dishonour the sacrifices of fallen military personnel. He made the pledge on Wednesday while formally taking over the leadership of the Board, promising to eliminate bureaucratic bottlenecks, deploy modern technology and streamline the processing of entitlements. Recalling his operational experience in Operation Hadin Kai in the North-East, Osifo said the military’s responsibility to its personnel extended beyond their years of active service to ensuring that their families were adequately supported after their death. He stressed that the sacrifices of personnel confronting security threats must be matched by an efficient pension administration system that guarantees prompt payment of entitlements to veterans and the families of fallen service members. Osifo said his administration would prioritise timely processing and payment of benefits while ensuring that legitimate beneficiaries received their entitlements without unnecessary delays. “My mission statement will be anchored on leading a Board that will prioritise all ways and means to ensure payments are prompt, accessed with seamless ease, less cumbersome, less bureaucratic, but with an overriding commitment to ensuring only the rightful recipients get their due entitlements,” he said. The new chairman assured military veterans and families of deceased personnel that his administration would improve access to benefits and reduce the difficulties associated with processing claims. He said the Board would adopt modern technology, strengthen collaboration with the military services to identify beneficiaries proactively and accelerate the processing of pensions, gratuities and death benefits. Osifo also pledged to deepen engagement with the Defence Headquarters, service headquarters, the Ministry of Defence, relevant National Assembly committees, the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation and the Ministry of Finance to improve coordination and facilitate payments. On staff welfare, he said the Board would invest in the capacity development and well-being of its military and civilian personnel, noting that a well-trained and motivated workforce was essential to efficient service delivery. He pledged to uphold high ethical and professional standards, strengthen training and ensure fair treatment of personnel. “The challenge to reposition the Board is a collective responsibility. In view of this, I implore all officers, servicemen and women, and civilian staff to brace up for the enormous task ahead. All hands must be on deck for the realisation of my vision,” he said. Osifo, the 26th officer to lead the institution, expressed gratitude to the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, for his appointment. He also acknowledged the Chief of Defence Staff and the Minister of Defence for approving his nomination. He commended his predecessors for laying the foundation for the Board’s development and paid tribute to his immediate predecessor and coursemate, Air Vice Marshal Mikhail Abdulraheem, for his service. Osifo pledged to build on previous administrations’ achievements and reposition the Board to provide prompt and efficient financial services to military retirees and the families of deceased personnel. In his valedictory remarks, Abdulraheem urged Board personnel to sustain teamwork, discipline and innovation to improve the welfare of military pensioners and their next-of-kin. He said the Board’s mandate transcended individual leadership, stressing that its success depended on the collective commitment of its personnel to the welfare of retired military personnel and their beneficiaries. “As I hand over leadership today, I urge you all to extend the same cooperation, respect, and commitment to my course mate. Give him your support, share your ideas freely, and continue to work as one team,” he said. “The mandate of this Board is greater than any individual, and its success depends on our ability to remain united and focused on the welfare of our military pensioners and their next-of-kin.” Abdulraheem thanked the officers, servicemen and women, and civilian staff for their cooperation, dedication and support throughout his tenure, attributing the Board’s achievements under his leadership to their collective efforts, professionalism and commitment to common goals. item.title: 2027: Opposition coalition closer to picking consensus candidate – G100
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The G-100 opposition coalition has intensified efforts to produce a consensus candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, inaugurating key committees to solidify its negotiations. Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja during the inauguration of the coalition’s Legal and Media Committees, National Chairman of the Social Democratic Party SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, disclosed that strategic engagements are progressing rapidly. Participating parties include the SDP, African Democratic Congress ADC, Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Peoples Redemption Party PRP, Peoples Democratic Party PDP, and Allied Peoples Movement APM. Prominent presidential hopefuls under consideration include Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Donald Duke, and Adewale Adebayo. Gombe noted that direct talks between party leaders and the aspirants are underway, with major breakthroughs expected before the end of the year. The newly established Legal Committee—composed of national legal advisers—will analyse constitutional frameworks, electoral laws, and Supreme Court rulings to safeguard the alliance against potential legal loopholes. Concurrently, the Media and Publicity Committee – comprising national publicity secretaries and campaign spokespersons – will manage joint communications and strategic messaging. Highlighting widespread economic hardship and security concerns under the current administration, Gombe emphasised that the coalition aims to provide a credible, unified alternative for Nigerians by prioritising national interest over individual political ambitions. The post 2027: Opposition coalition closer to picking consensus candidate – G100 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu meets with Zenith Bank founder Jim Ovia, Budget Office DG in Aso Villa
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu met on Tuesday with Jim Ovia, founder of Zenith Bank and chairman of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) at the Presidential Villa, Abuja. The President also met separately with the Director-General of the Budget Office of the Federation Tanimu Kurfi. Although no official reasons were given for the purposes of both meetings, Ovia arrived at the State House at about 2:15 p.m., dressed in his customary black suit and red tie. It was gathered that the Budget Office chief was on a regular briefing with the President and met him behind closed-doors. The Zenith Bank founder has chaired the NELFUND board since his appointment by President Tinubu on April 26, 2024. Ovia’s appointment came less than three weeks after President Tinubu signed into law the Access to Higher Education Act (Repeal and Re-Enactment) Act, which created the interest-free student-loan scheme. NELFUND provides an interest-free loan to eligible Nigerian tertiary and vocational students to cover approved educational costs. It is voluntary, applied for online, and repaid after graduation and employment through a capped income deduction. item.title: Dangote acquires 25% stake in Kenya pipeline
item.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, says his company has acquired a 25 per cent stake in Kenya Pipeline Company in a deal valued at approximately $327 million. Dangote announced the acquisition on Wednesday at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London, according to Reuters, saying the investment would facilitate the distribution of petroleum products. “We bought 25 per cent of their pipeline network for the distribution of petroleum products,” the president of Dangote Industries Limited said. The acquisition comes as Dangote expands his investments in Africa’s energy sector, including a proposed $16 billion refinery in Kenya designed to process 700,000 barrels of crude oil per day. On September 30, Dangote and Kenyan President William Ruto broke ground on the proposed refinery at Lamu Port. Dangote said the project would be commissioned within 40 months, adding that it would have a processing capacity comparable to his Nigerian refinery. “We will come back here and commission this refinery in 40 months from today. The East African refinery is designed to process approximately 700,000 barrels of crude per day. It will also generate 1,000 megawatts, twice that of Lagos,” he said. He added that the facility would produce one million tonnes of polypropylene and base oil, as well as supply at least 20 per cent of the jet fuel consumed in Europe and the United Kingdom. The pipeline acquisition follows Ruto’s announcement on Tuesday that private investors had acquired a 25 per cent stake in Kenya’s pipeline network from public entities. The Kenyan president did not identify the investors at the time. Earlier this year, Kenya sold a 65 per cent stake in Kenya Pipeline Company through an initial public offering, in a major privatisation move aimed at raising government revenue amid limited fiscal space. The transaction marked the country’s first major share sale in two decades. The post Dangote acquires 25% stake in Kenya pipeline appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Signal bug could keep your mic - and camera - on after hangup
item.description: Make sure you don’t say anything mean or secret after hanging up a call on Signal, as a bug in the encrypted messaging app’s calling library could prevent a call from ending properly, potentially leaving audio and possibly video active. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-113380 , was published by MITRE on Tuesday and given a CVSS score of 9.3, marking it as a critical issue in Signal’s open-source RingRTC library in every single version before 2.72.0. That update was pushed out last month, but the vulnerability wasn’t made public until now. RingRTC is Signal’s own calling library built on top of WebRTC , a technology introduced in 2011 that has since become widely used for voice and video communication over the internet. RingRTC provides Signal-specific calling functionality using WebRTC, which already encrypts media traffic, but that isn't stopping RingRTC from failing to hang up calls in certain conditions, according to the CVE report. What’s happening is, in essence, a denial-of-service attack on RingRTC’s finite state machine (FSM) event queue, which handles events involved in managing calls. If one of the people on the call saturates the FSM queue with requests, it can become overwhelmed and fail to process a hangup request, preventing the call from terminating properly. The vulnerability is classified as CWE-754 , or improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions, according to a report posted to GitHub. A conceptual proof of concept is available in the GitHub report linked above, using a Python script to simulate how flooding an event queue can prevent a hangup request from being processed. Were a malicious actor to exploit this, the person on the other end may think the call has been terminated, but either or both of their video and audio channels could still be open. The attack complexity is considered low according to the CVE, and while CISA’s known exploited vulnerabilities catalog doesn’t indicate this has been spotted in the wild, Signal users ought to ensure they’ve updated their apps - mobile and desktop - to the latest versions to ensure they don’t end up being caught on a hot mic without any notice. Comparing RingRTC 2.72.0 to the previous version indicates that Signal's fix allows the call's finite state machine (FSM) to detect termination requests independently of the event queue, while adding a timeout to prevent stalled processing from indefinitely blocking a hangup. It's not entirely clear from Signal's release notes when the fixed version of RingRTC reached the Android, iOS, and desktop versions of its apps. Signal Desktop's release history indicates that RingRTC 2.72.0 was incorporated in September, but the precise rollout dates across all platforms remain unclear. We’ve reached out to Signal to learn more, but haven’t heard back. In the meantime, best to update your installation to be sure you’re not still vulnerable. That, and watch what you say after hanging up a call. ®
item.dc:creator: Brandon Vigliarolo
item.content:encoded: Make sure you don’t say anything mean or secret after hanging up a call on Signal, as a bug in the encrypted messaging app’s calling library could prevent a call from ending properly, potentially leaving audio and possibly video active. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-113380 , was published by MITRE on Tuesday and given a CVSS score of 9.3, marking it as a critical issue in Signal’s open-source RingRTC library in every single version before 2.72.0. That update was pushed out last month, but the vulnerability wasn’t made public until now. RingRTC is Signal’s own calling library built on top of WebRTC , a technology introduced in 2011 that has since become widely used for voice and video communication over the internet. RingRTC provides Signal-specific calling functionality using WebRTC, which already encrypts media traffic, but that isn't stopping RingRTC from failing to hang up calls in certain conditions, according to the CVE report. What’s happening is, in essence, a denial-of-service attack on RingRTC’s finite state machine (FSM) event queue, which handles events involved in managing calls. If one of the people on the call saturates the FSM queue with requests, it can become overwhelmed and fail to process a hangup request, preventing the call from terminating properly. The vulnerability is classified as CWE-754 , or improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions, according to a report posted to GitHub. A conceptual proof of concept is available in the GitHub report linked above, using a Python script to simulate how flooding an event queue can prevent a hangup request from being processed. Were a malicious actor to exploit this, the person on the other end may think the call has been terminated, but either or both of their video and audio channels could still be open. The attack complexity is considered low according to the CVE, and while CISA’s known exploited vulnerabilities catalog doesn’t indicate this has been spotted in the wild, Signal users ought to ensure they’ve updated their apps - mobile and desktop - to the latest versions to ensure they don’t end up being caught on a hot mic without any notice. Comparing RingRTC 2.72.0 to the previous version indicates that Signal's fix allows the call's finite state machine (FSM) to detect termination requests independently of the event queue, while adding a timeout to prevent stalled processing from indefinitely blocking a hangup. It's not entirely clear from Signal's release notes when the fixed version of RingRTC reached the Android, iOS, and desktop versions of its apps. Signal Desktop's release history indicates that RingRTC 2.72.0 was incorporated in September, but the precise rollout dates across all platforms remain unclear. We’ve reached out to Signal to learn more, but haven’t heard back. In the meantime, best to update your installation to be sure you’re not still vulnerable. That, and watch what you say after hanging up a call. ®

item.title: Some climate damage is now unavoidable even if we clean up our act
item.description: Uros Arsic/AFP via Getty Images Thermometers, at least traditionally, don’t remember. Mercury expands in response to heat energy, and the red line rises. The temperature falls, the mercury contracts, the line descends. Yesterday’s measurement has no bearing on today’s. But even if thermometers can’t measure it, rising temperatures leave a lasting mark. Forests die, ice sheets melt and species go extinct. Now that the world is within touching distance of 1.5°C of warming, we are getting hints of the climate chaos we can expect over the coming century. So how bad will it be, and is the damage reversible? This isn’t just an abstract question. Last month, the United Nations finally acknowledged that holding warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels would only be possible if Earth overshoots that threshold, then cools back down by 2100. “Overshoot, peak, decline” is the new mantra for decision-makers. Let’s put aside, for the moment, the rather large question of how global cooling on this scale could be delivered. What lasting damage do we risk by overshooting? It is a question scientists are racing to answer. Advertisement There is some good news. Important land carbon sinks like the Amazon rainforest seem to be able to bounce back from short-term climate shocks. We may even be able to resuscitate the AMOC, a vital ocean current , after a climate-induced collapse – although it won’t be easy. When it comes to sea-level rise, we have locked ourselves in for a lot of future pain But the bad news is that some climate impacts are locked in, even if we clean up our act immediately. As we report, Thwaites glacier in Antarctica looks to be beyond saving , even if ocean-driven melting were halted overnight. In short, when it comes to sea-level rise, we have locked ourselves in for a lot of future pain. That isn’t a reason for despair. Once we pass 1.5°C of warming, we should double down on cutting emissions, not give up. But we should be aware that, even if we do successfully deliver global cooling, we won’t emerge from the overshoot years unscathed. What we do today matters for tomorrow.

item.title: Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ – Iran
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”. The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July. The Houthis seized much of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in September and have since launched attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on state oil giant Aramco and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed on October 10. Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. Sisi said Egypt was not seeking to “confront or attack anyone”, adding: “We are speaking only about defence.” AFP The post Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ – Iran appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Poor Network: Reps give MTN, Airtel, Glo, Mafab seven days
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Ad Hoc Committee investigating the persistent poor quality of telecommunications services in Nigeria has given the chief executive officers of MTN, Airtel, Globacom, Mafab Communications and other operators seven days to appear before it. The committee directed the telecom executives to appear on October 28, 2026, to explain the persistent deterioration in network quality and their failure to honour previous invitations. The ultimatum was issued at a public hearing in Abuja on Wednesday following the adoption of two motions sponsored by Reps. Sunday Umeha and Afam Ogene. The lawmakers expressed displeasure over the failure of invited operators, including MTN Nigeria and Mafab Communications, to appear before the committee as previously requested. Consequently, the committee directed the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to ensure that all affected operators comply with the invitation and appear at 2 p.m. on October 28 at Hearing Room 447 of the New Building of the National Assembly Complex, Abuja. The operators were also directed to submit all relevant documents to the committee on or before the scheduled date and explain the factors responsible for the persistent decline in service quality affecting millions of subscribers and businesses nationwide. The lawmakers warned that any chief executive who failed to honour the invitation could face a possible arrest summons to compel their appearance. Speaking at the hearing, the committee chairman, Rep. Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), said reliable telecommunications services had become critical to Nigeria’s economy, extending beyond voice calls and internet access to essential commercial activities, including Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Osoba noted that businesses, financial transactions and other essential services depended heavily on reliable telecommunications networks, making recurring service disruptions a matter of serious national concern. He said the House constituted the ad hoc committee to investigate persistent complaints by subscribers and establish the factors responsible for the poor quality of services provided by telecommunications operators. The chairman, however, expressed concern that the invited chief executives had continued to avoid direct engagement with the committee by offering various excuses or sending lower-ranking officials to represent them. He stressed that the committee expected the chief executives to appear personally, noting that they were better positioned to explain their companies’ operational challenges and commitments to improving service delivery. Also speaking, Rep. Ibe Osonwa criticised the operators for what he described as disregard for the House, despite the substantial revenue they generated from their operations in Nigeria. The lawmakers warned that any chief executive who failed to honour the invitation could face a possible arrest summons to compel their appearance. He said the House constituted the ad hoc committee to investigate persistent complaints by subscribers and establish the factors responsible for the poor quality of services provided by telecommunications operators. The chairman, however, expressed concern that the invited chief executives had continued to avoid direct engagement with the committee by offering various excuses or sending lower-ranking officials to represent them. He stressed that the committee expected the chief executives to appear personally, noting that they were better positioned to explain their companies’ operational challenges and commitments to improving service delivery. In his ruling, Osoba urged the NCC to ensure full compliance with the committee’s directive, reiterating that the affected operators must appear on October 28 with the required documents and explanations on the state of their networks. item.title: Food Security: Abiodun targets 10,000 farmers with subsidised inputs
item.description: Distributes 10 tractors, 1,200 smartphones to farmers Unveils 39 tractors, harvesters, agro-processing facilities Over 160,000 farmers, value-chain operators captured in state database ByClifford Ndujihe Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has stepped up efforts to boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses and improve farmers’ incomes, unveiling a fresh package of subsidised inputs, mechanisation equipment and digital tools targeting 10,000 rice and cassava farmers. The intervention, announced during the 2026 World Food Day celebration in Abeokuta, includes support for 2,000 rice farmers and 8,000 cassava farmers, the distribution of 10 tractors and 1,200 Android phones loaded with agricultural applications. Under the programme, each beneficiary will receive two bags of fertiliser and one bag of urea. Cassava farmers will also get 25 bundles of cassava stems and 10 litres of herbicides each, while rice farmers will receive three litres of herbicides. The state government said beneficiaries would pay 30 per cent of the cost of the inputs, with the government covering the remaining 70 per cent through its partnership with the International Fund for Agricultural Development, IFAD. The initiative is aimed at reducing farmers’ production costs and improving their capacity to increase output amid rising agricultural expenses and concerns over food affordability. Abiodun also disclosed that his administration had procured 39 tractors, four self-propelled harvesters and other agricultural equipment to strengthen mechanised farming across the state. The 1,200 smartphones distributed to farmers are equipped with applications providing weather information, market prices and guidance on improved farming practices. The digital intervention builds on the Ogun State Farmer Information Management System, launched in April 2023. According to the governor, more than 160,000 farmers and agricultural value-chain operators have been captured on the platform. Invests in processing, market access Special Adviser to the governor on Media, Mr Kayode Akinmade, said beyond farm inputs and machinery, the administration is investing in storage, processing and market access to reduce losses and improve returns to farmers. Abiodun said 28 agricultural projects had been completed in the preceding two years across crop production, aquaculture and poultry. They include solar dryers, warehouses, cassava processing centres and a poultry processing plant at Ajegunle Farm Settlement in Odeda Local Government Area. The poultry facility, according to the governor, has the capacity to process 5,000 birds daily, or about 1.3 million annually. Under the Ogun State Economic Transformation Project, OGSTEP, agribusiness firms have purchased more than 283,000 tonnes of agricultural produce, while farmer clusters have received capacity-building support and links to off-takers. The government has also partnered with Soilless Farm Lab to train more than 200 young people in soilless farmin

Under the programme, each beneficiary will receive two bags of fertiliser and one bag of urea. Cassava farmers will also get 25 bundles of cassava stems and 10 litres of herbicides each, while rice farmers will receive three litres of herbicides. The state government said beneficiaries would pay 30 per cent of the cost of the inputs, with the government covering the remaining 70 per cent through its partnership with the International Fund for Agricultural Development, IFAD. The initiative is aimed at reducing farmers’ production costs and improving their capacity to increase output amid rising agricultural expenses and concerns over food affordability. Abiodun also disclosed that his administration had procured 39 tractors, four self-propelled harvesters and other agricultural equipment to strengthen mechanised farming across the state. The 1,200 smartphones distributed to farmers are equipped with applications providing weather information, market prices and guidance on improved farming practices. The digital intervention builds on the Ogun State Farmer Information Management System, launched in April 2023. According to the governor, more than 160,000 farmers and agricultural value-chain operators have been captured on the platform. Invests in processing, market access Special Adviser to the governor on Media, Mr Kayode Akinmade, said beyond farm inputs and machinery, the administration is investing in storage, processing and market access to reduce losses and improve returns to farmers. Abiodun said 28 agricultural projects had been completed in the preceding two years across crop production, aquaculture and poultry. They include solar dryers, warehouses, cassava processing centres and a poultry processing plant at Ajegunle Farm Settlement in Odeda Local Government Area. The poultry facility, according to the governor, has the capacity to process 5,000 birds daily, or about 1.3 million annually. Under the Ogun State Economic Transformation Project, OGSTEP, agribusiness firms have purchased more than 283,000 tonnes of agricultural produce, while farmer clusters have received capacity-building support and links to off-takers. The government has also partnered with Soilless Farm Lab to train more than 200 young people in soilless farming and provide start-up support to beneficiaries. Abiodun said the Ogun State Agricultural Land Management Agency was established to facilitate access to agricultural land and promote investment in commercial farming. Speaking at the event, a former Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Professor Kolawole Adebayo, said Ogun had approximately 1.2 million hectares of arable land, offering significant potential for agricultural production and agro-industrial development. Adebayo called for sustained investment in innovation and an integrated transport network linking rail, road, water and air transport to ease the movement of agricultural produce and preserve its quality. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Bolu Owotomo, stressed the importance of ensuring access to nutritious and affordable food, calling for greater investment in women and young people through improved access to land, finance, training and technology. Owotomo disclosed that more than 12,000 farmers had benefited from training and agricultural inputs under OGSTEP. The state government said it would continue to complement federal agricultural interventions through farmer support, investment and stronger market linkages. However, the impact of the initiatives will depend on timely distribution of inputs, effective maintenance of equipment, transparent beneficiary selection and improved access to markets. Higher yields, lower production costs, better farmers’ incomes and reduced post-harvest losses will ultimately determine whether the investments translate into sustained food security and more affordable food for consumers. item.title: 'Cyberpunk 2077' is getting a huge new co-op mod
item.description: Night City is having a busy week. Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a major 2.5 update on Oct. 22, coinciding with the recent release of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 anime. CD Projekt Red just confirmed what’s in 2.5, including new quests, a perk that enables dual wielding, console mod support, and more. However, the game is arguably getting an even bigger update through unofficial channels: Cyberpunk 2077 is receiving multiplayer co-op support via the NightCoop mod.

item.title: 5 Nollywood Movies to Watch on Streaming Platforms Before October Ends
item.description: Toyin Abraham’s directorial comedy drama Oversabi Aunty is now streaming on Netflix and Kava. Your next movie night could take you from a hilarious Nollywood comedy to a fantasy world full of adventure, or straight into a crime story that keeps you guessing. With several Nollywood films and series now available to stream, there’s plenty to add to your watchlist before October wraps up. Whether you’re in the mood for a box-office hit you missed at the cinema or a moving coming-of-age story, these are the titles worth making time for. Oversabi Aunty (Streaming on Kava TV and Netflix) Toyin Abraham ’s record-breaking directorial debut follows Toun, a self-righteous church usher whose overzealous obsession with fixing everyone else’s morals turns her home and family life into a chaotic battlefield. Her relentless meddling reaches its breaking point during a disastrous family introduction, forcing her to confront the emotional fallout and damage she has caused her loved ones. Directed, written, and produced by Toyin Abraham alongside FilmOne Studios, the witty dramedy features an ensemble cast including Toyin Abraham, Mike Ezuruonye , Jemima Osunde , Tana Adelana , Efe Irele , Enioluwa Adeoluwa , and Queen Nwokoye . Colours of Fire (Streaming on Netflix) Niyi Akinmolayan ’s epic fantasy film takes viewers into an ancient world where the fabric-weaving Blue Tribe and the mysterious Red Tribe maintain a bitter, generational conflict. When a warrior named Akinbode is sent to eliminate a beast terrorising his people, his unexpected encounter with Moremi—the daughter of the Red Tribe’s queen—ignites a forbidden romance that challenges inherited stories and threatens to unravel their entire society. Directed and written by Niyi Akinmolayan, with production credits from Anthill Studios, FilmOne Studios, and Imuetinyan Productions, the visually rich film stars Uzor Arukwe , Osas Ighodaro , Mercy Aigbe , Gabriel Afolayan , Femi Branch , and Ibrahim Chatta . Ordinary People (Streaming on Netflix) Moses Inwang ’s crime thriller series dives deep into the gritty, interconnected lives of characters navigating power, ambition, and survival across the streets of Lagos and beyond. The story exposes how everyday decisions spiral into high-stakes consequences when ordinary individuals find themselves caught in webbed conflicts and dangerous secrets. Created, directed, and written by Moses Inwang, the eight-episode production features a powerhouse cast starring Ramsey Nouah , Adunni Ade , Chidi Mokeme , Sharon Ooja , Michelle Dede , Shawn Faqua , Lasisi Elenu , Uche Montana , and Jackie Appiah . Where Is Mr Right? (Streaming on Prime Video) Tunde Olaoye ’s romantic drama follows Bunmi, an event planner facing immense societal and familial pressure to get married before crossing an arbitrary age milestone. Her determined quest to locate an ideal partner spirals into a series of comedic missteps, unexpected heartbreaks, and lessons on patience and self-discovery. Directed

item.title: Ebola: NCDC holds emergency meeting to conclude action plans
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has convened an emergency meeting and commenced coordinated response activities following the Federal Government’s declaration of an Ebola outbreak in the country. The agency disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X page on Wednesday, saying the meeting brought together its leadership and key partners to coordinate the response. “The first Incident Management Meeting was convened on October 21, 2026, after the Honorable Minister’s official outbreak declaration of Ebola in Nigeria, bringing together leadership and key partners to align on response efforts,” the NCDC said. The agency also announced that its Incident Action Plan was being finalised, while response teams had commenced field operations focusing on surveillance, contact tracing and infection prevention. “The Incident Action Plan is being finalized today; NCDC teams are on the ground conducting case management and response activities, prioritising enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and coordinated risk communication,” the statement read. Reaffirming its commitment to containing the outbreak, the agency said, “We remain committed to a timely, coordinated, and evidence-based response to safeguard the health of Nigerians.” The Federal Government confirmed Nigeria’s first Ebola virus disease case on Tuesday after laboratory tests returned positive in the Federal Capital Territory. The patient, a woman who recently travelled from Uganda on an international flight, reportedly received treatment at a private hospital for several days before the infection was confirmed. She has since been placed in isolation. The post Ebola: NCDC holds emergency meeting to conclude action plans appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. The post Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NASA to Conduct NCAA Flyover, Engage Fans at University of Alabama
item.description: NASA’s Freedom 250 F-5 team, including NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, performs a flyover during the national anthem at an NFL game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers at Huntington Bank Field, Sept. 27, 2026, in Cleveland. NASA/Jordan Cochran As part of the agency’s Inspiration Tour, NASA will conduct a flyover at the University of Alabama vs. Texas A&M football game in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, on Saturday, Oct. 24. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F-5 fighter jets during the flyover, highlighting NASA’s contributions to aeronautics and the agency’s continued commitment to advancing aviation technologies. Ahead of the game, members of the news media are invited to visit the NASA Experience Zone on Champions Lane, where Isaacman will participate in a media opportunity at 11 a.m. CDT. Media interested in attending should confirm their attendance by 12 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23, with Lance D. Davis at lance.d.davis@nasa.gov to receive additional details and instructions. Supported by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, the NASA Experience Zone will be open to the public from 10:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. CDT, with no game ticket required. The experience will give visitors an opportunity to meet NASA team members and learn more about the people and technologies advancing the agency’s missions in aeronautics and space exploration. Attendees can engage with NASA team members and explore exhibits highlighting the agency’s Artemis campaign and efforts to return astronauts to the Moon, including: An inflatable SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. Displays featuring the Starship and Blue Moon human landing systems. Information about NASA internship opportunities. Photo opportunities featuring NASA exhibits and displays. With stops across the nation, NASA’s Inspiration Tour convenes academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders to connect the agency with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space. The tour will culminate in MAX POWER, a public exposition of American air and space innovation, Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8, on and near the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Held in honor of America’s historic 250th anniversary, the multi-day, family-friendly event will showcase the next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles, and technologies that will help define the future of transportation in air and space. For more information about MAX POWER and the agency’s missions, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/maxpower -end- Lance D. item.title: Nigeria loses ₦1.13tn yearly to foreign cloud dependency — Study
item.description: Experts downplay fears of AI-driven job losses By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Nigeria loses about $850 million, equivalent to ₦1.13 trillion, annually through its reliance on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies, according to research commissioned by global technology philanthropy Luminate. The Chief Executive Officer of Luminate, Melanie Hui, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Build 2026 Conference, convened by the Nigeria Artificial Intelligence (AI) Collective. In her address, titled “Africa in the Global AI Order: Towards Equitable Ownership and Shared Prosperity,” Hui said the country’s dependence on foreign cloud infrastructure raised questions about digital ownership and the distribution of economic value. “Nigeria, like countries across the world, relies heavily on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies. The research we commissioned estimates that this dependency costs Nigeria around $850 million each year,” she said. Hui stressed that hosting digital infrastructure within a country’s borders did not necessarily translate into ownership or control. “A country does not own its digital future when a data centre merely sits within its borders. The more important questions are who controls it, who can afford to use it, what powers it, whose data it processes and where the resulting economic value flows,” she said. She also drew attention to the historical inequalities reflected in Africa’s digital infrastructure, noting that the fibre-optic cables carrying the continent’s internet traffic followed some routes associated with historic injustice. “Infrastructure, indeed, encodes relationships of power. It determines who connects to whom, who controls the gates, who pays rent, and who extracts value,” she said. According to Hui, Africans should not be confined to subordinate roles in the global AI economy. “My African friends tell me they will not be confined to the role of consumer, supplier of raw data, source of critical minerals or provider of low-paid labour in somebody else’s AI economy,” she said. On data governance, she warned against treating people and communities merely as sources of information from which technology companies could generate products and profits. “People and communities must not be treated as reservoirs of data from which others fashion their products, profits and ideas,” she said. Hui also rejected arguments that regulation necessarily slows technological progress, insisting that safeguards were essential to responsible innovation. “Those of us who promote tech justice must not lend credence to some, in the tech industry, who would paint regulation as a brake on progress. I disagree. Safeguards are the allies of progress,” she said. item.content:encoded: Experts downplay fears of AI-driven job losses By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Nigeria loses about $850 million, equivalent to ₦1.13 trillion, annually through its reliance on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies, according to research commissioned by global technology philanthropy Luminate. The Chief Executive Officer of Luminate, Melanie Hui, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Build 2026 Conference, convened by the Nigeria Artificial Intelligence (AI) Collective. In her address, titled “Africa in the Global AI Order: Towards Equitable Ownership and Shared Prosperity,” Hui said the country’s dependence on foreign cloud infrastructure raised questions about digital ownership and the distribution of economic value. “Nigeria, like countries across the world, relies heavily on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies. The research we commissioned estimates that this dependency costs Nigeria around $850 million each year,” she said. Hui stressed that hosting digital infrastructure within a country’s borders did not necessarily translate into ownership or control. “A country does not own its digital future when a data centre merely sits within its borders. The more important questions are who controls it, who can afford to use it, what powers it, whose data it processes and where the resulting economic value flows,” she said. She also drew attention to the historical inequalities reflected in Africa’s digital infrastructure, noting that the fibre-optic cables carrying the continent’s internet traffic followed some routes associated with historic injustice. “Infrastructure, indeed, encodes relationships of power. It determines who connects to whom, who controls the gates, who pays rent, and who extracts value,” she said. According to Hui, Africans should not be confined to subordinate roles in the global AI economy. “My African friends tell me they will not be confined to the role of consumer, supplier of raw data, source of critical minerals or provider of low-paid labour in somebody else’s AI economy,” she said. On data governance, she warned against treating people and communities merely as sources of information from which technology companies could generate products and profits. “People and communities must not be treated as reservoirs of data from which others fashion their products, profits and ideas,” she said. Hui also rejected arguments that regulation necessarily slows technological progress, insisting that safeguards were essential to responsible innovation. “Those of us who promote tech justice must not lend credence to some, in the tech industry, who would paint regulation as a brake on progress. I disagree. Safeguards are the allies of progress,” she said. Citing examples of efforts to hold technology companies accountable, she referenced the Nigerian competition authority’s action against Meta over alleged data exploitation and discriminatory practices. She also noted that app-based drivers in Nigeria had secured government recognition for what she described as Africa’s first e-hailing trade union. Hui called for an AI economy rooted in African agency, capabilities and innovation, where prosperity would be measured not only by market size but also by the opportunities and freedoms available to people. Experts Say AI Could Create More Jobs At the conference, technology experts also sought to allay fears that artificial intelligence would lead to widespread job losses, arguing that the technology could create new employment opportunities and improve productivity. Their comments came amid warnings by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank about AI’s potential impact on the global labour market. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva recently described AI as a “slow-moving tsunami” at the “Small AI: More and Better Jobs” event during the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. She said about 40 per cent of jobs globally could be augmented, downgraded or eliminated by the technology. World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, meanwhile, has emphasised the need to ensure that development translates into employment, arguing that AI should improve productivity and support job creation rather than simply replace workers. However, the Chief Executive Officer of Data Science Nigeria, Dr Olubayi Adekanmbi, argued that the overall gains from AI could outweigh the losses. “There is something we call net effect. Some wins and some losses. But by the time you weigh them together, you will realise that the net effect of AI is going to be much more. Because many jobs that never existed before, AI will make them possible,” he said. Adekanmbi maintained that human judgement would remain important even as AI tools became increasingly integrated into professional work. “AI can help in my diagnosis, but the final decision will still come from doctors. So, a doctor can reach out to more people faster because the doctor has used AI. It’s never taking the job of a doctor. That is why everybody must learn AI so that when you learn AI with your current job, you will not lose your job,” he said. He urged workers to acquire AI skills and learn how to apply the technology within their existing professions. Digital Skills Key to Job Creation The Executive Director of the Policy Innovation Centre and host of the Nigeria AI Collective Secretariat, Dr Osasuyi Dirisu, said digital skills development would be critical to creating jobs for Nigeria’s young population. “We have a very young demographic in Nigeria. In order to create jobs at scale, we need to leverage digital technology. We need to leverage digital jobs, and one of the ways to do that is to build digital skills,” she said. Dirisu said young Nigerians needed to be prepared for emerging employment opportunities through training and continuous skills development. She described the Nigeria AI Collective as “a community of practice that is working to build an ethical and inclusive future for AI development in Nigeria.” Experts Address AI-Generated Election Falsehoods The conference also examined concerns over the use of AI to spread misinformation, disinformation and deepfakes ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dirisu said the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), a partner of the Collective, was working to address the threat through election-monitoring labs and media training. Adekanmbi, however, said AI tools could also help Nigerians verify information and counter falsehoods. “Somebody posts something, and you ask Grok, ‘Please confirm,’ Grok can immediately crawl the internet for you and confirm it,” he said. He proposed extending such verification services to Nigerians without internet access through telephone-based systems. “They can use maybe a mobile phone to call a number and say that ‘I heard something,’ and immediately they can get a response telling them that what you heard is not true. The technology for that already exists,” he said. The post Nigeria loses ₦1.13tn yearly to foreign cloud dependency — Study appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New 'Pokémon' Release Reinvents The Series' Most Hated Monster Type
item.description: Every Pokémon type has its own fandom, but the least popular element has to be bug-type. No offense to any self-described Bug Catchers out there, but a category of monsters based on insects — which many people fear or loathe in real life — was never destined to be a community favorite. When you factor in the monster type's many weaknesses , and what you get is an underappreciated class of Pokémon.

item.title: Websites go dark worldwide as AI exposes critical security flaws
item.description: Government agencies and companies around the world shut down websites Wednesday after two critical flaws came to light involving PHP, a programming language that is the basis for a large share of the internet. The US National Security Agency told organizations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline. The flaws “often provide a direct path to the server’s file system or database,” the NSA said in a statement on X. Attackers could use them to take over web servers without needing a password. PHP sits underneath popular web design platforms so the weaknesses potentially affect a vast range of websites, from online stores and news outlets to government services. The discovery came amid a surge in software security disclosures driven by increasingly powerful AI models, with the number of vulnerabilities found in 2026 on track to roughly double last year’s record total. PHP volunteers released a fix on Wednesday. “If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now,” the PHP Foundation, which funds developers working on the language, said in a blog post. The flaws were reported in August by security firm Calif and by ChatGPT maker OpenAI, which flagged them independently on the same day. Google-owned cloud security company Wiz later reported further ways to exploit them. The flaws had been reported privately to PHP’s developers at the time and kept confidential while a fix was prepared. Details leaked online Tuesday, a day before the planned release, prompting the rush to take sites offline. In France, local government websites, including the Paris Police Prefecture, have been inaccessible since Wednesday afternoon at the request of the French National Cybersecurity Agency, following “detection of a critical security vulnerability,” the Ministry of the Interior said. In the Netherlands, the national digital identity service DigiD, the website of the House of Representatives and the site of the national cybersecurity center went offline as a precaution, according to Dutch public broadcaster NOS. Belgium’s foreign ministry temporarily took its websites offline as a precaution, it said on X, although the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium had recorded no attacks on Belgian sites. AFP The post Websites go dark worldwide as AI exposes critical security flaws appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How to play DMZ solo in Modern Warfare 4
item.description: A lot of people are wondering how to play DMZ solo in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , or even whether it's actually possible in the first place. I bring good news: it is definitely possible, but the setting is a little hidden, and chances are, you'll load into your first game without even seeing the option not to party up with other random solo players.

item.title: Game Pass Is Losing a Legendary Point-and-Click Masterpiece This Halloween
item.description: It's been a tough few months for Xbox , with waves of layoffs, studio closures, and the prospect of outrageously expensive next-gen hardware looming. But Xbox Game Pass continues to chug along, welcoming a wave of new games twice a month while bidding farewell to other titles in the library. There's one classic title leaving the service on Oct. 31 that you won't want to miss — and it's a short game that's a perfect fit for spooky season: 2016's Day of the Tentacle Remastered.

item.title: World set to breach 1.5°C warming limit set by Paris Climate Agreement
item.description: The UN is warning that global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals of 1.5 degrees Celsius warming – and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century. The report by the United Nations Environment Programme lays bare the chasm between rhetoric and action when it comes to tackling global warming, and the challenge before political leaders at November's COP31 climate summit - set to take place next month in Turkey. Story by Emerald Maxwell.

The image was acquired with its Left Navigation Camera on Oct. 11, 2026 (Sol 2006) at a local mean solar time of 14:40:39. NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Vandi Verma, Chief Engineer for Robotic Operations at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory Oct. 12, 2026 Since the last blog update, Perseverance has achieved a major milestone on Mars. On Sol 2006 (Oct. 11, 2026), its odometer reached 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles), setting a new record for the farthest distance driven on another celestial body. Its engineering twin here on Earth even received a plaque from Guinness World Records celebrating the achievement. Two months ago, on Sol 1947, the odometer sat about 200 meters away from the milestone, a distance easily achievable with a single drive using Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav). However, the rover found itself in a very scientifically interesting area and spent time executing short drives to perform rock abrasions and proximity science on ancient rock outcrops. When Perseverance was finally ready to move on to a new site, it sailed past the record. On its way to the drive record, Perseverance has navigated challenging terrain while also pioneering new ways to drive across the Martian surface. Perseverance’s various encounters with dense boulder fields and steep slopes have pushed the team to re-evaluate driving guidelines so the rover is better prepared to handle tough terrain. After running thousands of simulations, the team raised the rover’s tilt limit to 24 degrees and reduced the clearance required under the rover’s belly pan to 20 centimeters (about 7.9 inches). The team also updated the rover’s braking software to avoid rock hazards, nearly doubled steer motor current limits, updated flight software with “dynamic slip tables” to model expected slip, and used cross-slope driving to better anchor wheels on exposed bedrock. One of the most exciting updates the team has made is an autonomous drive capability called onboard Global Localization (GBLC). item.content:encoded: Explore This Section Perseverance Home Mission Overview Rover Components Mars Rock Samples Where is Perseverance? Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Mission Updates Science Overview Objectives Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Perseverance Raw Images Images Videos Audio More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home This image, taken by Perseverance on Mars, shows wheel tracks from the drive that broke the record for the farthest distance driven on another celestial body. The image was acquired with its Left Navigation Camera on Oct. 11, 2026 (Sol 2006) at a local mean solar time of 14:40:39. NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Vandi Verma, Chief Engineer for Robotic Operations at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory Oct. 12, 2026 Since the last blog update, Perseverance has achieved a major milestone on Mars. On Sol 2006 (Oct. 11, 2026), its odometer reached 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles), setting a new record for the farthest distance driven on another celestial body. Its engineering twin here on Earth even received a plaque from Guinness World Records celebrating the achievement. Two months ago, on Sol 1947, the odometer sat about 200 meters away from the milestone, a distance easily achievable with a single drive using Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav). However, the rover found itself in a very scientifically interesting area and spent time executing short drives to perform rock abrasions and proximity science on ancient rock outcrops. When Perseverance was finally ready to move on to a new site, it sailed past the record. On its way to the drive record, Perseverance has navigated challenging terrain while also pioneering new ways to drive across the Martian surface. Perseverance’s various encounters with dense boulder fields and steep slopes have pushed the team to re-evaluate driving guidelines so the rover is better prepared to handle tough terrain. After running thousands of simulations, the team raised the rover’s tilt limit to 24 degrees and reduced the clearance required under the rover’s belly pan to 20 centimeters (about 7.9 inches). The team also updated the rover’s braking software to avoid rock hazards, nearly doubled steer motor current limits, updated flight software with “dynamic slip tables” to model expected slip, and used cross-slope driving to better anchor wheels on exposed bedrock. One of the most exciting updates the team has made is an autonomous drive capability called onboard Global Localization (GBLC). GBLC repurposes the high-speed commercial processor inside the Ingenuity Helicopter Base Station to compare ground and orbital imagery to autonomously locate the rover in global coordinates at the end of a drive (as though we had GPS on a world without it), enabling Perseverance to drive longer distances without human intervention. Unlike Perseverance’s main flight computer, this coprocessor is not hardened against the punishing radiation environment of the Martian surface, where a thin atmosphere and the lack of a global magnetosphere leave little shielding. This radiation can induce “transient bit flips” in memory the software needs to function, and the team developed an effective software-based approach to radiation hardening. Looking forward to the greater demands of longer drives and to planning more activity with fewer resources, the team is also exploring the use of generative SI to help efficiently propose solutions to steer AutoNav along the many legs of a strategic path. The team is using hard-won lessons from 45 kilometers (more than 28 miles) of driving to reinvent how the rover drives across the Martian surface. As Perseverance climbs higher along the crater rim, the next leap in autonomous exploration on Mars is just getting started. Want to read more posts from the Perseverance team? item.title: OpenBSD 8.0 beefs up virtual machines and gets a taste of Wine
item.description: OpenBSD 8.0 brings bigger virtual machines, graphics improvements, and another helping of AI mockery. The round version number doesn't signal a radical break with its predecessors. OpenBSD 8.0 is the 61st release of the project. Developer Bryan Steele posted a highlights rundown on Mastodon. Wireless improvements include updates to the qwx driver for Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6 hardware. Its VMM/VMD hypervisor now supports multiprocessor VMs with up to 64 virtual CPUs in each guest. The kernel virtual memory address space on x86-64 is now 512 GB, up from 4 GB, allowing for GPUs with large amounts of VRAM. On Arm64 machines, OpenBSD supports hibernation, and on both x86-64 and Arm64 it can use CPU AES instructions for faster encrypted swap. Component upgrades include OpenSSH 10.6 and LibreSSL 4.4.0, and the DRM graphics driver stack from Linux 6.18. The default C compiler is Clang/LLVM 22, including for the SPARC64 edition – but at the cost of dropping support for the Loongson architecture. The list of errata is short, with just four fixes – but then, version 8.0 is very new. Just days before this release, there was a high-profile OpenBSD issue: Calif's "Big Fish" research describes a decades-old shared-memory bug chained with a separate kernel flaw to gain local root access. Both were fixed in OpenBSD 7.9 , through errata 026 and 018 respectively. Project leader Theo de Raadt forked OpenBSD from NetBSD 1.0 in 1995, and the first release of the new OS was OpenBSD 1.2 in July 1996 – so version 8.0 is as close as the project will get to a 30th anniversary release. According to Calif's proof-of-concept code on GitHub , the bug was in the original code that both OpenBSD and NetBSD inherited from the original BSD codebase – which is how come there's a 37-year-old bug in a 30-year-old project. A HackerNews comment says: "Interestingly, looks like this was accidentally fixed in NetBSD during a rewrite of that code in August of 1999." The project has not updated its infamous slogan. The homepage still proclaims: "Only two remote holes in the default install, in a heck of a long time!" As we noted in May when OpenBSD 7.9 appeared , the project rejects code generated by LLMs, although on the basis of licensing concerns rather than its cousin NetBSD's explicit anti-AI stance . As we reported recently , this strict anti-AI stance seems to be serving NetBSD well. OpenBSD is also an anti-AI project, and for this release, the website goes out of its way to make that very clear. OpenBSD's mascot is a pufferfish, and in the banner artwork for the new release, "Puffy" has an extra eye – and the signpost in the image's background also has malformed text, a hallmark of early image-generation bots. The eyes are also constantly blinking – one at a time – to emphasize that this is a reference to Blinky the mutant fish from The Simpsons. In case you missed The Simpsons reference, the version 8.0 release theme song makes it even more explicit: it's titled "The Simps on AI." The lyri
item.dc:creator: Liam Proven
item.content:encoded: OpenBSD 8.0 brings bigger virtual machines, graphics improvements, and another helping of AI mockery. The round version number doesn't signal a radical break with its predecessors. OpenBSD 8.0 is the 61st release of the project. Developer Bryan Steele posted a highlights rundown on Mastodon. Wireless improvements include updates to the qwx driver for Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6 hardware. Its VMM/VMD hypervisor now supports multiprocessor VMs with up to 64 virtual CPUs in each guest. The kernel virtual memory address space on x86-64 is now 512 GB, up from 4 GB, allowing for GPUs with large amounts of VRAM. On Arm64 machines, OpenBSD supports hibernation, and on both x86-64 and Arm64 it can use CPU AES instructions for faster encrypted swap. Component upgrades include OpenSSH 10.6 and LibreSSL 4.4.0, and the DRM graphics driver stack from Linux 6.18. The default C compiler is Clang/LLVM 22, including for the SPARC64 edition – but at the cost of dropping support for the Loongson architecture. The list of errata is short, with just four fixes – but then, version 8.0 is very new. Just days before this release, there was a high-profile OpenBSD issue: Calif's "Big Fish" research describes a decades-old shared-memory bug chained with a separate kernel flaw to gain local root access. Both were fixed in OpenBSD 7.9 , through errata 026 and 018 respectively. Project leader Theo de Raadt forked OpenBSD from NetBSD 1.0 in 1995, and the first release of the new OS was OpenBSD 1.2 in July 1996 – so version 8.0 is as close as the project will get to a 30th anniversary release. According to Calif's proof-of-concept code on GitHub , the bug was in the original code that both OpenBSD and NetBSD inherited from the original BSD codebase – which is how come there's a 37-year-old bug in a 30-year-old project. A HackerNews comment says: "Interestingly, looks like this was accidentally fixed in NetBSD during a rewrite of that code in August of 1999." The project has not updated its infamous slogan. The homepage still proclaims: "Only two remote holes in the default install, in a heck of a long time!" As we noted in May when OpenBSD 7.9 appeared , the project rejects code generated by LLMs, although on the basis of licensing concerns rather than its cousin NetBSD's explicit anti-AI stance . As we reported recently , this strict anti-AI stance seems to be serving NetBSD well. OpenBSD is also an anti-AI project, and for this release, the website goes out of its way to make that very clear. OpenBSD's mascot is a pufferfish, and in the banner artwork for the new release, "Puffy" has an extra eye – and the signpost in the image's background also has malformed text, a hallmark of early image-generation bots. The eyes are also constantly blinking – one at a time – to emphasize that this is a reference to Blinky the mutant fish from The Simpsons. In case you missed The Simpsons reference, the version 8.0 release theme song makes it even more explicit: it's titled "The Simps on AI." The lyrics and the vocals parody both Simpsons characters and AI users. Our favorite line sounds like Grampa Simpson, and says: Back in my day we didn't have artificial intelligence, we had real stupidity – and we liked it. We've seen negative reactions online, but then we often find that some people lack much of a sense of humor. For our part, we really enjoyed seeing the OpenBSD team having such fun. We reckon it will appeal to many Butlerian Jihadi types. It certainly did to The Reg FOSS desk. A little Wine with your pufferfish A couple of days before the 8.0 release came an unexpected announcement on the openbsd-ports mailing list: a proposed port of Wine for OpenBSD . This is a new version of the Wine 11 runtime that allows Windows binaries to launch and run on OpenBSD. This is a 64-bit version of Wine for OpenBSD on x86-64, and for now, this means it can only run 64-bit Windows code. (For the technical nitty-gritty: Wine needs to manipulate the CPU's GS register. Windows on x86-64 uses the GS segment base to locate the Thread Environment Block (TEB), as the late great Geoff Chappell explained . This is a very longstanding Windows data structure, going all the way back through Windows 95 to OS/2 . The port was particularly tricky because OpenBSD doesn't allow programs to alter that, so the port is emulating instructions that use the %gs segment override. The snags are that this means 32-bit code doesn't work, and secondly, because this is unnecessary on Linux, the code is unlikely to be merged back into upstream Wine.) If you want to see it working, there are a few screenshot galleries on Reddit's openbsd_gaming group, showing a number of recent major titles running: Some samples from WIP wine port , more wine-on-OpenBSD screenshots , and even more wine-on-OpenBSD proof . The port comes hedged with caveats, notable among them that Wine does not do any kind of sandboxing, so using it potentially opens up OpenBSD to Windows malware. However, for some users, this could be a very useful addition. OpenBSD is the simplest and cleanest member of the BSD family, indeed, of the FOSS Unix family. Part of this is because entire subsystems are missing that the other BSDs provide. Bluetooth connections to Apple's wireless keyboards and pointing devices aren't supported. There's no logical volume management – which would massively help with OpenBSD's complex disk partitioning. There's no journaling filesystem either (although a port of the new Gefs is in progress ). While small and clean, its priorities favor security and simplicity, though performance will depend on the hardware and workload. Importantly – since you probably will need to ask for help – the OpenBSD community does not have a reputation for friendliness. Saying that, it is quite a lot easier to get OpenBSD installed and running, complete with its 25-year-old version 2.2.5 of the Fvwm window manager , than either NetBSD or FreeBSD. If you're looking for an AI-free, and indeed systemd-free, path away from Linux, OpenBSD 8.0 is very definitely worth a try. ®

item.title: [VIDEO] ‘This Govt Has Normalised Lack Of Empathy,’ Rhodes-Vivour Condemns Use Of Tear Gas At #EndSARS Anniversary
item.description: The candidate of the African Democratic Party (ADC) for the February 16, 2027, governorship election in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has condemned the use of tear gas canisters during the sixth anniversary of #EndSARS at the Lekki Toll Gate. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Wednesday, Rhodes-Vivour accused the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government of normalising the lack of empathy for Nigerians who lost their lives during the October 2020 protest against police brutality. “They are normalising this bullying system of governance that has come to describe what the APC government has become, and the citizen is going to have to really understand what is at stake here because we need a government that actually understands that lives were lost on this day,” he said. “Innocent citizens were killed.” ﻿ The post [VIDEO] ‘This Govt Has Normalised Lack Of Empathy,’ Rhodes-Vivour Condemns Use Of Tear Gas At #EndSARS Anniversary appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: France: Far right leader Marine Le Pen gains popularity amid nationwide riots
item.description: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met with union leaders today in France. His government admitted law enforcement officers had lost control this past weekend during protests which resulted in scenes of violence and looting. The country is bracing for more protests – the Yellow Vest movement called on demonstrators to take to the street on Saturday. As the events unfold, far-right leader Marine Le Pen is gaining popularity. Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi.

item.title: 70% of water produced in Guadeloupe never reaches homes
item.description: In the French overseas territory of Guadeloupe, a water crisis is a daily reality, with some residents going without water for weeks. The network is being repaired, but at the current pace, France's Court of Auditors says replacing all of it would take 208 years. Now, a judicial investigation has been opened in Paris into the crisis, following a citizen-led legal action. Our France 2 colleagues report.

item.title: Students Hospitalised After Fresh Methane Emission In Two Ogun LGAs
item.description: Many secondary school students have been hospitalised following a fresh outbreak of methane emission in Ijebu-Ode, Ijebu-Igbo and Ago-Iwoye in Ogun State. The incident occurred on Wednesday morning, affecting students of Anglican Girls Grammar School, including its public and private sections, in Obalende, Ijebu-Ode, as well as Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School. ﻿ Several students were taken to the general hospitals in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo for medical attention, while the odour disrupted academic activities in Ago-Iwoye, prompting some schools to close abruptly and send pupils home. The incident triggered panic among parents, guardians and teachers, some of whom rushed to hospitals to check on the condition of the affected students. However, the General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency (OGEPA), Kehinde Bello, who was on the ground to assess the situation in Ijebu-Ode and that of Ijebu-Igbo, disclosed that the latest occurrence was linked to underground gas emissions previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April 2026. Bello stated that the state government was working on the situation with the aim of finding a lasting solution. He said government investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. He urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. “We left the General Hospital earlier, where over 30 students were attended to for common symptoms, according to the doctor, and the findings from the affected students include shortness of breath, stomach disorder, drowsiness, among others. “While some of them needed oxygen to be stabilised, others just needed minor medical attention. As at the time we were leaving the hospital, most of the students had been discharged, but a few are still under monitoring,” he said. “We are presently at Ijebu Igbo Girls Grammar School for assessment and further investigations. We also checked the surrounding area. This odour was not peculiar to the schools alone; those in the environs were also affected. “The Ijebu North LG Chairman also confirmed that he perceived the odour at the LG secretariat too,” Bello added. Meanwhile, residents who were exposed to the odour have been advised to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. The latest incident has renewed concerns over the recurrence of methane emissions in the affected communities, particularly their impact on schools and the safety of children. The Ogun State Government in June attributed the methane emissions recorded in some schools in Ijebu-Ode to natural underground ecological causes, dismissing speculations linking the incidents to spiritual myths or security threats. The Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said scientific investigations identified methane and sulphide gases as the major emissions

The incident triggered panic among parents, guardians and teachers, some of whom rushed to hospitals to check on the condition of the affected students. However, the General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency (OGEPA), Kehinde Bello, who was on the ground to assess the situation in Ijebu-Ode and that of Ijebu-Igbo, disclosed that the latest occurrence was linked to underground gas emissions previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April 2026. Bello stated that the state government was working on the situation with the aim of finding a lasting solution. He urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. “We left the General Hospital earlier, where over 30 students were attended to for common symptoms, according to the doctor, and the findings from the affected students include shortness of breath, stomach disorder, drowsiness, among others. “While some of them needed oxygen to be stabilised, others just needed minor medical attention. As at the time we were leaving the hospital, most of the students had been discharged, but a few are still under monitoring,” he said. “We are presently at Ijebu Igbo Girls Grammar School for assessment and further investigations. We also checked the surrounding area. This odour was not peculiar to the schools alone; those in the environs were also affected. “The Ijebu North LG Chairman also confirmed that he perceived the odour at the LG secretariat too,” Bello added. Meanwhile, residents who were exposed to the odour have been advised to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. The latest incident has renewed concerns over the recurrence of methane emissions in the affected communities, particularly their impact on schools and the safety of children. The Ogun State Government in June attributed the methane emissions recorded in some schools in Ijebu-Ode to natural underground ecological causes, dismissing speculations linking the incidents to spiritual myths or security threats. The Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said scientific investigations identified methane and sulphide gases as the major emissions escaping through underground fractures along established fault lines. The affected areas, according to Oresanya, fall within the Ifewara-Zungeru Trans-Atlantic fault line, which stretches from Mojoda through Ijebu-Ode to Osun and Niger states. He also noted that the affected part of Ijebu-Ode was historically forested and largely uninhabited before missionary schools were established there.
